title: Don't leak AliasPath keys into model_extra in model_construct
body:
## Change Summary

`model_construct` pops field names and `str` validation aliases out of the input dict before assigning the leftovers to `__pydantic_extra__`, but the `AliasPath` branch only read via `search_dict_for_path` without removing anything. With `extra='allow'`, the alias path's root key leaked into `model_extra` (and could shadow the field's own value in `model_dump`).

The fix records each consumed `AliasPath` root during the field loop and removes those keys from `values` after all fields have been processed, before `_extra` is assigned. Deferring the removal (rather than popping inline) keeps fields that share a path root working, matching `model_validate` behavior. The caller's input is never mutated (`values` is a fresh kwargs dict).

## Related issue number

Fixes #13869

title: perf: avoid Python tuple round trip between ModelFieldsValidator and ModelValidator
body:
## Change Summary

For every model instance, `ModelFieldsValidator::validate` packed `(model_dict, model_extra, fields_set)` into a Python tuple, and `ModelValidator` immediately extracted the three values again — a wasted allocation plus extraction per model.

This exposes the validated components through a new `ModelFieldsValidator::validate_fields` method (returning the existing `ValidatedModelFields` tuple type directly), and `ModelValidator` now calls it when its inner validator is a bare `ModelFields` validator. Wrapped validators (function-before/wrap) and standalone `model-fields` schemas still go through `Validator::validate`, so the tuple contract there is unchanged.

## Related issue number

Fixes #13927

## Benchmark

Release build, single-field model, 1M validations x7 runs (median): ~1.53M validations/sec vs ~1.20M/sec before the change (+27%).

title: Fix non-init fields with validate_assignment=True on Pydantic dataclasses
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->
## Change Summary

Support non-init fields without defaults in Pydantic dataclasses when `validate_assignment=True`.

Previously, dataclass fields with `init=False` and no default value or default factory were skipped during field collection in `collect_dataclass_fields`. As a result, `__pydantic_fields__` did not contain them. When `validate_assignment=True` was configured, setting such fields (for instance, inside `__post_init__`) triggered `__pydantic_validator__.validate_assignment`, raising an `AttributeError: 'X' object has no attribute 'x'` because the attribute was not yet set on the instance.

This PR addresses the issue by:
1. Collecting `init=False` dataclass fields in `collect_dataclass_fields` so they are properly registered in `__pydantic_fields__`.
2. Updating dataclass schema generation field sorting in `_generate_schema.py` to ensure `init=False` fields are sorted after `init=True` positional fields, preserving the expected `__init__` signature.
3. Catching `AttributeError` during assignment validation in `validated_setattr` and setting the attribute via `object.__setattr__` if the field exists in `__pydantic_fields__`.

## Related issue number

fix #5470

title: Fix datetime parsing in custom validator examples
body:
## Change Summary

The custom datetime-validator examples inspect `tzinfo` or `utcoffset()` before the datetime handler parses the input. As a result, an ISO datetime string raises `AttributeError`, including when supplied through `TypeAdapter.validate_json()`.

This only changes `docs/examples/custom_validators.md`.

title: Skip the generic pickle test when cloudpickle is absent

labels.name: relnotes-ignore
labels.description: Omit this PR from the release notes.

body:
## Change Summary

`test_generic_model_pickle_different_module` fails with `IndexError: list index out of range` in an environment that does not have `cloudpickle` installed.

The test spawns a subprocess whose code does `import cloudpickle`. `cloudpickle` is declared in the `testing-extra` dependency group rather than `dev` ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/pyproject.toml)), so it is absent from a default environment. The child then dies before printing anything, and the parent fails at `creator.stdout.splitlines()[0]` on an empty stdout, an error that gives no indication of its cause.

This skips the test when `cloudpickle` is unavailable, using the same guard [tests/test_pickle.py](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/tests/test_pickle.py) already uses for this exact dependency: the import is skipped outright on PyPy, and otherwise guarded with `try`/`except ImportError`. Both halves matter. `importlib.util.find_spec` was the shorter alternative and was avoided deliberately, because it reports a package that is on disk yet fails to import as present. And PyPy has to be excluded up front rather than caught, because there `import cloudpickle` raises `AttributeError` rather than `ImportError`, so a `try`/`except ImportError` does not contain it, and since the import happens at module level during collection, the failure surfaces as a collection error for the whole file before any `skipif` is consulted.

It also asserts the subprocess return code, so a failure from any other cause (a pydantic / pydantic-core version skew between parent and child, a syntax error in the generated code, or a timeout) reports itself instead of surfacing as the same opaque `IndexError`.

### A note on the PyPy failure this initially introduced

The first version of this PR guarded the import with `try`/`except ImportError` only, and passed every check available on CPython. CI caught that it is not enough: on PyPy, `import cloudpickle` raises `AttributeError: type object 'Pickler' has no attribute 'dispatch'`, which that guard does not catch, and because the import is at module level the failure became a collection error for the whole file. The guard now mirrors `test_pickle.py` in full, and the PyPy path is therefore the one that file already exercises.

### Verification

The failure reproduces on a checkout without `testing-extra`, and was confirmed to come from the child's import by capturing its stderr:

```text
subprocess returncode : 1
subprocess stderr     : ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cloudpickle'
subprocess stdout     : ''          # so .splitlines()[0] raises IndexError
```

Results for `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/pydantic_core --ignore=tests/mypy`:

| environment | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without `cloudpickle` | `1 failed, 6184 passed` | `6184 passed, 28 xfailed` |
| with `cloudpickle` | `6207 passed` | `6207 passed, 28 xfailed` |

`tests/test_generics.py` specifically: `122 passed, 4 xfailed` without it (only this test skips, the rest of the module still runs), `123 passed, 4 xfailed` with it.

`ruff check .` and `ruff format --check` are clean. The change is confined to `tests/test_generics.py`; no production code is touched.

## Related issue number

None. This corrects a test-harness failure rather than a defect in `pydantic`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for an issue first unless the change is trivial. This is a 13-line, test-only guard with no behaviour change, so I read it as falling under that exemption. Happy to open an issue if that is the wrong call.

* [x] Unit tests for the changes exist
* [x] Tests pass on CI
* [ ] Documentation reflects the changes where applicable

Concretely: the diagnosis was found by running the suite, the patch was written by the agent, and it was then reviewed by a separate adversarial review pass, which raised three points that were addressed: the comment's placement between two decorators, `find_spec` versus the `try`/`except ImportError` idiom already used in `test_pickle.py`, and the unchecked subprocess return code.

title: feat: support attribute docstrings inheritance for TypedDict and dataclasses
body:
## Change Summary

When `use_attribute_docstrings=True` is enabled, attribute docstrings declared on base classes were previously dropped for `TypedDict` subclasses and dataclasses because docstring extraction only inspected the leaf class rather than traversing the class hierarchy.

This PR adds inheritance support for attribute docstrings:
1. In `_update_fields_from_docstrings` (`pydantic/_internal/_fields.py`), traverse `reversed(cls.__mro__)` so dataclasses inherit attribute docstrings from base classes while allowing subclasses to override them.
2. In `_generate_schema.py`, traverse `reversed(mro(typed_dict_cls))` (using Pydantic's virtual MRO for `TypedDict`) so inherited `TypedDict` fields retain docstrings from parent `TypedDict`s and can override them.
3. Remove the `@pytest.mark.xfail` marker from `test_stdlib_docs_extraction_inheritance()` in `tests/test_docs_extraction.py`.
4. Add comprehensive unit tests covering Pydantic dataclass inheritance, `TypedDict` inheritance, and `TypedDict` docstring overrides.
5. Update documentation warning in `pydantic/config.py` to reflect that inheritance is now supported for `TypedDict` and dataclasses.

## Related issue number

References #13468. Addresses the inheritance limitation tracked by the `test_stdlib_docs_extraction_inheritance` xfail test.

title: Perf: Avoid the Python tuple round trip between `ModelFieldsValidator` and `ModelValidator`
body:

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything

For every model instance, `ModelFieldsValidator::validate` packs `(model_dict, model_extra, fields_set)` into a Python

body:
As `model_construct()` bypasses validation, it doesn't try to rebuild the model first if it is incomplete. This could cause issues with serialization inference (fixed differently in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/13922), but also when using referring to `FieldInfo` attributes such as `alias`, as per this failing test:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/5c2a929726717b9a98575e245a180a082f1b7d26/tests/test_construction.py#L674-L694

As such, we should try to rebuild the model before using `model_construct()` (only doable in v3).

title: Rebuild incomplete types during serialization inference

labels.name: relnotes-fix
labels.description: Used for bugfixes.

body:
I was skeptical if this was a good idea (at first, it felt weird to have potential errors related to failed resolution of forward references raised during serialization), but we already do this during validation anyway, and the potential error raised is strictly better that the confusing `TypeError: 'MockValSer' object cannot be converted to 'SchemaSerializer'` one we have today.

We don't provide any namespace depth on purpose, to avoid resolving types from unrelated places, so if it succeeds it should be guaranteed to resolve types properly.

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7713.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13647.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12282 (already closed as duplicate).

title: fix: inherit TypedDict closed/extra_items from parent classes (PEP 728)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #13919.

PEP 728 `closed`/`extra_items` support was added in #12179, but three cases from the spec don't work:

1. **`extra_items` not inherited** — A subclass of a TypedDict with `extra_items=int` should also accept extra int items. Pydantic treats the subclass as a plain TypedDict and silently drops the extra keys.

2. **`closed=True` not inherited** — A subclass of a closed TypedDict should also reject extra keys. Pydantic accepts them and drops them instead of raising `extra_forbidden`.

3. **`extra_items=Never` and `extra_items=ReadOnly[int]` fail** — These raise `PydanticSchemaGenerationError`. Per PEP 728, `extra_items=Never` is the same as `closed=True`, and `extra_items` can be wrapped in `ReadOnly[]`.

## Root Cause

In `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`, `__closed__` and `__extra_items__` are read directly from the class. Per PEP 728, those attributes only reflect what was passed to that exact class, not its parents. TypedDict parents are in `__orig_bases__`, not `__mro__`.

## Fix

In `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`:
- Walk `__orig_bases__` to find inherited `__closed__` and `__extra_items__` values from parent TypedDicts
- Handle `extra_items=Never` as equivalent to `closed=True`
- Unwrap `ReadOnly[]` from `extra_items` before passing to `generate_schema`

## Changes

- `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`: Inheritance walk + `Never`/`ReadOnly` handling
- `tests/test_types_typeddict.py`: 4 new regression tests

## Verification

- 4 new tests: RED before fix, GREEN after fix
- All 84 TypedDict tests pass
- Full `test_types.py`: 280 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed
- `ruff check pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`: All checks passed

### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

PEP 728 support was added in #12179, but a few cases from the spec don't work.

1. `extra_items` isn't inherited. A subclass of a TypedDict with `extra_items=int`
should also accept extra int items. Pydantic treats the subclass as a plain TypedDict
and silently drops the extra keys.

2. `closed=True` isn't inherited. A subclass of a closed TypedDict should also reject
extra keys. Pydantic accepts them and drops them instead of raising `extra_forbidden`.

This also affects JSON schema: the parent gets `"additionalProperties": false`,
the subclass doesn't.

3. `extra_items=Never` and `extra_items=ReadOnly[int]` raise
`PydanticSchemaGenerationError`. The PEP says `extra_items=Never` is the same as
`closed=True`, and allows `extra_items` to be wrapped in `ReadOnly[]`.

For 1 and 2, I think the cause is that `_generate_schema.py` reads `__closed__` and
`__extra_items__` directly from the class. Per the PEP, those attributes only reflect
what was passed to that exact class, not its parents. TypedDict parents also aren't
in `__mro__`, only in `__orig_bases__`, so finding the inherited value means walking
those.

For 3, `extra_items` is passed straight to `generate_schema` without handling
`Never` or unwrapping `ReadOnly`.

I'd like to work on a fix for this if that's okay.

### Example Code

```Python
import json
from typing import Never

from typing_extensions import ReadOnly, TypedDict

from pydantic import TypeAdapter


class Parent(TypedDict, extra_items=int):
    a: str


class Child(Parent):
    pass


print(TypeAdapter(Parent).validate_python({'a': 'x', 'b': '1'}))
# {'a': 'x', 'b': 1}
print(TypeAdapter(Child).validate_python({'a': 'x', 'b': '1'}))
# {'a': 'x'}  expected {'a': 'x', 'b': 1}


class ClosedParent(TypedDict, closed=True):
    a: str


class ClosedChild(ClosedParent):
    pass


print(TypeAdapter(ClosedChild).validate_python({'a': 'x', 'b': 1}))
# {'a': 'x'}  expected ValidationError

print(json.dumps(TypeAdapter(ClosedParent).json_schema()))
# includes "additionalProperties": false
print(json.dumps(TypeAdapter(ClosedChild).json_schema()))
# missing "additionalProperties": false

TypeAdapter(TypedDict('TD', {'a': str}, extra_items=Never))
# PydanticSchemaGenerationError
TypeAdapter(TypedDict('TD', {'a': str}, extra_items=ReadOnly[int]))
# PydanticSchemaGenerationError
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```Text
pydantic version: 2.13.5
        pydantic-core version: 2.46.5
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.13.7 (tags/v3.13.7:bcee1c3, Aug 14 2025, 14:15:11) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)]
                     platform: Windows-11-10.0.26100-SP0
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: unknown

Also reproduced on Linux with Python 3.15.0b4 and pydantic main (2.14.0b2).
```

Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

title: Handle OS errors during `ZoneInfo` validation
body: Fixes #13908. Validating a ZoneInfo field with a tzdata directory name ('America', 'Etc') or an over-long key raises a raw OSError subclass instead of ValidationError, so a user-supplied timezone can crash e.g. a web API with an unhandled exception. Root cause: validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz only catches (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, TypeError), but ZoneInfo() hits the filesystem and raises OSError subclasses for these inputs (IsADirectoryError on POSIX / PermissionError on Windows for directory names on Python < 3.13 per CPython gh-85702; ENAMETOOLONG / EINVAL for over-long keys - I reproduced both cases, including the Windows PermissionError variant). Fix: catch OSError alongside the existing exceptions so all invalid keys surface as zoneinfo_str errors. Single call site, no behavior change for valid zones. Tests: new parametrized test_zoneinfo_parsing_fails_for_os_errors in tests/test_types_zoneinfo.py asserting the full error shape for both cases. Verified: all 9 tests in the file pass on Python 3.11 with tzdata installed; ruff check and format clean. (The one test_datetime.py timedelta failure also fails on pristine main in this env - pre-existing, unrelated.)

title: `ZoneInfo` validation raises `IsADirectoryError`/`OSError` instead of `ValidationError` for some invalid keys
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Validating a `ZoneInfo` field with certain invalid strings raises a raw `OSError` subclass instead of a `ValidationError`:

- A tz database *directory* name such as `'America'`, `'Europe'` or `'Etc'` raises `IsADirectoryError` on Python 3.10–3.12 when the `tzdata` package is installed (`tzdata` is a pydantic dependency on Windows and is also pulled in by e.g. pandas). CPython only started converting this case to `ZoneInfoNotFoundError` in 3.13 (gh-85702).
- An over-long key (e.g. 300 characters) raises `OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long` (reproduced on Python 3.12 with `tzdata`, and on Python 3.13 on macOS without it).

`validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz` in `pydantic/_internal/_validators.py` only catches `(ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, TypeError)`, so these errors propagate unchanged. Expected: a `zoneinfo_str` validation error, the same as for `'Not/AZone'`. For example, in a web API that validates a user-supplied timezone, these inputs currently produce an unhandled exception instead of a validation error.

Suggested fix: add `OSError` to the caught exceptions. I have a small patch with a regression test ready if this is welcome.

### Example Code

```python
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Model(BaseModel):
    tz: ZoneInfo

Model(tz='Not/AZone')  # ValidationError (expected)
Model(tz='America')    # IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.../site-packages/tzdata/zoneinfo/America'
Model(tz='a' * 300)    # OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long: '...'
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```
             pydantic version: 2.14.0b2
        pydantic-core version: 2.49.0
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 11 2026, 03:55:21) [Clang 22.1.3 ]
                     platform: macOS-15.3.1-arm64-arm-64bit
             related packages: email-validator-2.3.0 typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: e2ac21dcd
```
(tzdata is installed in this environment)

Disclosure: found, reproduced and the draft fix tested locally with the help of an AI coding agent (Claude Code); reviewed before filing.

Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

title: Explicitly enable frame pointers
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

[PEP 831](https://peps.python.org/pep-0831/) ([What's New in 3.15](https://docs.python.org/3.15/whatsnew/3.15.html#whatsnew315-frame-pointers)): starting with Python 3.15, CPython is built by default with [`-fno-omit-frame-pointer`](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangCommandLineReference.html#cmdoption-clang-fomit-frame-pointer) and [`-mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer`](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/x86-Options.html#index-mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer-3), i.e. frame pointers are kept in every function, including leaf functions (functions that don't call anything else).

These flags are exposed through [`sysconfig`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/sysconfig.html#sysconfig.get_config_var), so C extensions built by tools that read Python's build configuration (e.g. setuptools) inherit them automatically. For everything else, the What's New entry says:

> Build systems that compile C, C++, Rust, or other native code without inheriting Python's compiler flags should enable equivalent frame-pointer flags themselves. A single native component built without frame pointers can break stack unwinding for the whole Python process.

### Where Rust / PyO3 / maturin stand

- `rustc` doesn't read `sysconfig` flags. maturin, PyO3's build scripts and maturin-action don't add frame-pointer flags either. Until now, pydantic-core got rustc's per-target default.
- That default is controlled by [`-C force-frame-pointers`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/codegen-options/index.html#force-frame-pointers) and depends on the target. As of rustc 1.97.1:

  | Target | Default | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | [`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/targets/aarch64_unknown_linux_gnu.rs#L22) | kept in non-leaf functions | [rust-lang/rust#140832](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/140832): the [AArch64 procedure call standard](https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/4492d1570eb70c8fd146623e0db65b2d241f12e7/aapcs64/aapcs64.rst#the-frame-pointer) lets each platform define frame-pointer requirements. [Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms) and [Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/arm64-windows-abi-conventions?view=msvc-170) mandate them; for Linux, Rust follows clang (non-leaf). |
  | Apple [`x86_64` / `aarch64`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/base/apple/mod.rs#L153-L159) | always / non-leaf | Follows Apple platform conventions. |
  | [`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/targets/x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu.rs) | **may omit** | No override, so it uses the [global default](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/mod.rs#L2854). Enabling non-leaf frame pointers everywhere was benchmarked in [rust-lang/rust#115521](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/115521) and judged "a pretty hard sell" performance-wise; it's still unmerged. |

- The prebuilt Rust standard library shipped by [rustup](https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/) *is* built with `-Cforce-frame-pointers=non-leaf` ([`[profile.dist]` in `library/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/library/Cargo.toml#L60-L73)), so std frames don't break the chain. Only our own code does.

**Net effect before this PR:** on x86_64 Linux (the most common deployment target), a profiler walking the stack of a 3.15 process loses the chain as soon as it enters `_pydantic_core`. On aarch64 Linux and macOS it mostly works already (except in leaf functions).

### This PR

Adds `-C force-frame-pointers=yes` to `pydantic-core/.cargo/config.toml` for all targets except wasm ([Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/) builds, where native profilers don't apply):

- It is a [`target.'cfg(...)'`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targetcfgrustflags) entry rather than [`build.rustflags`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustflags), because Cargo ignores `build.rustflags` as soon as any `target.*` entry matches, and our existing macOS [`target.<triple>`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustflags) entries would silently disable it. Matching `target.<triple>` and `target.<cfg>` entries are joined together. The wasm exclusion uses [`target_family`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#r-cfg.target_family).
- `yes` rather than `non-leaf`: `non-leaf` requires `-Zunstable-options`, which only works on nightly. `yes` also matches CPython, which keeps frame pointers in leaf functions too.
- Checked locally (aarch64 macOS): `maturin build -v` passes the flag alongside the macOS link args, and maturin's PGO flags are [appended to the configured rustflags](https://github.com/PyO3/maturin/blob/4c4d695109ef2799d6331681f9cafbccc4722bac/src/compile.rs#L427-L446) rather than replacing them. As with any config rustflags, setting `RUSTFLAGS` (e.g. `make build-coverage`) overrides them.

### Performance

The only target where this meaningfully changes codegen is x86_64 Linux, which is also where Rust decided the cost wasn't worth making it the default. CodSpeed runs on x86_64 Linux, so its results on this PR show the actual cost for pydantic-core.

title: Fix config propagation of stdlib dataclasses and `TypedDict`s in JSON Schema

labels.name: topic-json schema
labels.description: Related to JSON Schema

labels.name: relnotes-fix
labels.description: Used for bugfixes.

labels.name: needs-blogpost-entry
labels.description: This PR needs to be documented in the release notes blog post

body:
## Summary

Stdlib dataclasses and `TypedDict`s without their own config inherit the parent config (see [configuration propagation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/concepts/config/#configuration-propagation)). Core schema generation already does this, but JSON Schema generation pushed an empty config (`{}`) for these types instead of `None`, so they didn't inherit it. As a result, the JSON Schema didn't match validation or serialization behavior.

The parent config is now inherited when generating the JSON Schema of these types. If the type has its own config, it is still used. Class-level JSON Schema settings (`title`, `json_schema_extra`, etc.) from the parent are still not applied.

## Examples

Validation:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

from typing_extensions import TypedDict

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


@dataclass
class DC:
    name: str


class TD(TypedDict):
    name: str


class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_max_length=5)

    dc: DC
    td: TD


Model(dc={'name': 'too long'}, td={'name': 'too long'})
#> ValidationError: 2 validation errors (for `dc.name` and `td.name`)

print(Model.model_json_schema()['$defs']['DC']['properties']['name'])
# Before: {'title': 'Name', 'type': 'string'}
# After:  {'maxLength': 5, 'title': 'Name', 'type': 'string'}
# (Same for `TD`)

Separate JSON and Python validation paths for IP types in lax mode.

Previously, lax JSON validation reused the Python validator, which allowed numeric JSON inputs to be accepted by Python's `ipaddress` constructors even though the generated JSON Schema declares these values as strings.

This change makes lax JSON validation accept strings only, while preserving the existing Python lax coercion behavior, including integer inputs where supported.

The behavior is covered for all IP types using `_ip_schema()`:
- `IPv4Address`
- `IPv6Address`
- `IPv4Interface`
- `IPv6Interface`
- `IPv4Network`
- `IPv6Network`

## Related issue number

fix #13888

title: fix: reflect Field(init=False) in dataclass metadata
body:
## Change

`as_dataclass_field()` converts a Pydantic `FieldInfo` into a stdlib `dataclasses.field()`, but it dropped the `init` argument — so a field declared with `Field(init=False)` still carried `init=True` in the dataclass metadata.

That had three observable consequences (reproduced on 2.13.5 and `main`):

- the excluded field appeared in `__init__` and `__match_args__`, so positional pattern matching bound the wrong value;
- `dataclasses.replace()` fed the field back into the constructor and raised `unexpected_keyword_argument` under `extra='forbid'`;
- replacing `Field` with `dataclasses.field` in the same example worked, confirming the drop was in the Pydantic-to-stdlib conversion.

This propagates `pydantic_field.init` when set, mirroring how `kw_only` and `repr` are already handled. The `init` default (`None` → stdlib `True`) is untouched, so fields without an explicit `init` behave exactly as before.

## Regression test

`test_init_false_reflected_in_dataclass_metadata` in `tests/test_dataclasses.py`, parametrized over both `pydantic.Field` and `dataclasses.field`, asserts:

- `dataclasses.fields()` reports `init=False` for the excluded field and `True` for the rest;
- `__match_args__` excludes it;
- `dataclasses.replace()` succeeds without feeding the field back into `__init__`.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/test_dataclasses.py -q` → 268 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- `uv run ruff check pydantic/_internal/_dataclasses.py tests/test_dataclasses.py` → clean.

Fixes #13833.

title: fix: stdlib dataclass JSON schema inherits parent model's extra config
body:
`dataclass_schema()` used `getattr(cls, '__pydantic_config__', {})` — an empty-dict fallback — which caused `_config_wrapper_stack.push({})` to silently replace the enclosing model's config with an empty one. `generate_inner()` would then see no `extra='forbid'` and skip emitting `additionalProperties: false`, even when the parent `BaseModel` had `extra='forbid'`.

**Reproduction:**
```python
import dataclasses
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic.config import ConfigDict

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Inner:
    x: int

class Outer(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    inner: Inner

schema = Outer.model_json_schema()
# Before fix: Inner schema has no `additionalProperties: false`
# After fix:  Inner schema correctly includes `additionalProperties: false`
```

**Fix:** pass `None` when the class has no `__pydantic_config__` so that `push(None)` is a no-op and the parent config is preserved. Then derive `config` for `_update_class_schema` from the effective stack tail when `own_config` is absent.

The validation path in `_generate_schema.py` already applies this pattern (PR #10928). This PR applies the same fix to the JSON-schema path.

Fixes #13845

title: Validate json models straight off the jiter cursor
body:
## Change Summary

`validate_json` builds the whole document into a `JsonValue` tree and then walks it. For a model schema the tree is pure overhead: the shape is known in advance, so the document can be read once, straight onto python objects.

This is the "validation by iteration" step #12550 was groundwork for, and what #10032 describes wanting.

A plan is derived from the schema saying how each field's value can be taken — a string, bool, int or float whose json type matches exactly, a nested model, a list or dict to any depth, and null for anything nullable. `nullable` and `default` are seen through, single-key aliases resolve with the same priority rule as the ordinary path, and `extra='forbid'` is fine because an unknown key simply hands the object back.

**Nothing about it is meant to be observable.** Anything the cursor cannot finish exactly is re-read from its own bytes and validated normally. No leaf validator is reimplemented, and every error a user sees is still built by the ordinary path, with its own message and location — there is no error-construction code on this path at all.

## Numbers

Instructions, measured against the tree path in the same binary, on real pydantic models over the corpora serde_json/simdjson/orjson benchmark on:

| document | |
|---|---|
| canada (111k coordinates) | **−43.0%** |
| twitter | −27.6% |
| product catalog | −27.0% |
| event log | −27.7% |
| citm_catalog | −22.0% |

Wall clock tracks it (canada −41%), peak RSS drops 2–10 MB, and `from_json` is unchanged at ±0.08% as a control.

## Why this is safe to turn on

On by default, because the fallback is what makes it invisible. `PYDANTIC_DISABLE_JSON_STREAMING` switches it off — an escape hatch rather than a feature flag, and how the differential test reaches the tree path.

Four independent checks:

1. **A `stream-verify` build** (`--features stream-verify`) runs the ordinary path alongside every streamed call and compares the results structurally. Turning pydantic's whole suite into a differential test of this path is the strongest evidence here.
2. **A differential test** (`tests/test_streaming_json.py`) runs the same schemas and documents down both paths and compares values, attribute order, fields-set and the full error list. Each side runs in its own process, and **every case asserts `_stream_plan_accepted`** — a differential test passes trivially if the fast path never engaged, and forcing the plan to refuse turns 13 of 15 cases red.
3. **6,026 pydantic-core tests and 12,898 pydantic tests** pass with it on, and unchanged with it off.
4. Oracles over generated documents, and `model_dump_json` equality over the corpora.

## Commits

The first is an independent refactor and could land on its own: it shares the alias priority rule between the two places that read an object, so the streamed path cannot drift from the tree path's rule. The last three are separately measured optimisations, each with its number in the message.

## What it declines

Falls back to the tree path for `by_alias`, `by_name`, `allow_partial`, an explicit `extra_behavior`, or `self_instance`; and per-object for any value whose json type is not exactly what the field wants, or a missing field with no default.

## Notes for review

- **The `stream-verify` build validates twice**, so two tests that count validator invocations (`test_validate_json_context` in `tests/test_main.py` and `tests/test_type_adapter.py`) fail under it. They pass on an ordinary build with streaming on. Same shape as a checking build double-running anything that counts calls.
- **One cost is jiter's to remove.** Skipping a value finds its end without decoding, so invalid utf-8 inside a field the model ignores was being accepted where the tree path rejects it — on jiter main, `next_skip` returns `Ok` for `{"a": "\xff"}` where `JsonValue::parse` errors. Skipped spans are now checked here, which costs the one document whose model ignores most of its bytes ~9%. Fixing it in jiter would make the check free, since the skip already reads those bytes.

title: Harden the pure-annotation schema caches: a key collision, a retention bound, and a checking mode
body:
## Change Summary

Three additions to #13544, stacked so they can be merged into it directly. One is a correctness fix, one answers the open review comment on #13542, and one is the evidence for both. Targeting `field-fast-path` because the changes span both PRs' code.

### 1. `Tuple` and `Tuple[()]` must not share a cache entry

Both have `tuple` as their origin and an empty `get_args()`, so `pure_annotation_cache_key()` returns `(tuple,)` for each — but bare `Tuple` is a variadic tuple of anything and `Tuple[()]` is the empty tuple, and their schemas differ by `variadic_item_index`. Whichever is built first decides what the other one validates.

`tests/test_edge_cases.py::test_pep585_generic_types` **fails on `field-fast-path` when run on its own** (both parametrizations); the full suite happens to build the two forms in the order that hides it. Confirmed to be the caches: forcing them to decline makes it pass.

The two are told apart by whether the alias carries `__args__` at all.

### 2. Bound what a cache key retains, not just how many there are

`CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT` caps the number of entries, but a key can hold a `str`, `bytes` or `int` of any size and is retained until the cache is reset. The reviewer comment on #13542 reported this for `Literal` values; measuring found **three more paths** with the same behaviour:

| path | 8 models × a distinct 1 MB value | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Literal` values | 8.00 MB retained | 0 |
| `str`/`bytes` defaults | 8.00 MB | 0 |
| strings inside encoded metadata | 8.00 MB | 0 |
| `alias`/`title`/`description` in the field-schema key | 8.00 MB | 0 |

The last one matters most in practice — every OpenAPI-documented field has a description, and it goes into the key as it is. `int` is included because python integers are unbounded (`10 ** 1_000_000` as a default is over 400 KB).

A value that large is unique to its field, so its entry would never have been reused; refusing it costs nothing. Measured on the shapes in #13545, the extra length check is within noise.

### 3. A checking mode, and the edge cases it exposed

`PYDANTIC_VERIFY_SCHEMA_CACHE=1` builds every field schema a second time with the caches emptied and compares the two structurally, reporting totals at the end of the run:

```
schema caches: 21,923 field schemas checked against an uncached build, 0 differed
```

It lives in the test suite, not in `pydantic/`, so it costs the shipped diff nothing — emptying the cache dicts in place is enough to force the long way round. **This is what found the `Tuple` collision above.**

Plus 110 edge-case tests, each checked by removing the guard it covers and confirming it goes red:

- **99 combinations of config setting × pure annotation**, comparing generated schemas with the cache cleared in between. The "no configuration can affect a pure annotation's schema" claim currently holds for all of them; this is what fails if a future setting breaks it. (Worth noting for anyone writing more: `str_strip_whitespace` is invisible here because it goes through the model's core config, and an enum under `use_enum_values` carries a `ref` — `arbitrary_types_allowed` is one that does reach a schema.)
- a hook monkeypatched onto a trusted leaf class **after** it has been cached, and an in-place mutation of `AnyUrl._constraints` — both already handled correctly, neither previously pinned down
- one `Field()` reused by two models, equal mutable defaults not being shared, `Literal` over an enum member not treated as pure

## Validation

- `12,470 passed`, plus one pre-existing environment failure (`test_exports.py::test_public_internal`, a mypy plugin version clash)
- checking mode: 21,923 field schemas, 0 differed
- **free-threaded 3.14t**: all 169 cache tests pass; a 16-thread × 250-model stress test (4,000 models, caches hitting their size limit so the clear-then-assign path runs under contention) reports zero problems over three runs. Shown non-vacuous: collapsing `Literal` keys makes one thread receive another's schema.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean

## A note on the numbers

Measured against the merge-base as a separate checkout (not by disabling the caches from inside the branch, which flatters them — a disabled-but-still-storing baseline pays for work it never uses):

| | main | branch | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 600 models × 3 `Optional[str]` | 447 ms | 319 ms | −28.8% |
| mixed field shapes | 505 ms | 391 ms | −22.6% |
| `Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10)]` | 659 ms | 517 ms | −21.6% |
| `import mcp` (50 pairs) | 1226 ms | 1200 ms | +2.1% |
| `import fastmcp` (50 pairs) | 596 ms | 595 ms | nothing |

Consistent with the caveat in #13545: the win is on per-model class-definition time, and whole-library imports dilute it. `import fastmcp` is only ~37% model definition.

## Known gaps

- `typing.Any` is in `_PURE_LEAF_TYPES` and, since 3.11, is a mutable python class — `Any.__get_pydantic_core_schema__ = ...` sticks, so "immutable C types only" is not quite true and a hook on `Any` would be reachable. Obscure, and closing it costs a lookup on the hottest path or moving `Any` into the verified-leaf map; left alone deliberately.
- Three existing tests count `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` invocations and so fail under the checking mode, which builds twice. They are deselected when running it rather than modified:
  `tests/test_annotated.py::test_modify_get_schema_annotated`,
  `tests/test_internal.py::test_trusted_leaf_class_rejects_monkeypatched_hook`,
  `tests/test_main.py::test_get_core_schema_unpacks_refs_for_source_type`.

title: Fix #13817: remove double-visitation of validator tree in ValidatorCallable and ValidatorIterator
body:
Hey, this fixes the GC crash reported in #13817.

Long story short: when you use a `mode='wrap'` field validator and the handler outlives the validation call (which happens when a ValidationError keeps it alive in its traceback), Python's GC ends up traversing the validator tree twice. Once through the parent validator's `impl_py_gc_traverse!`, and once through `ValidatorCallable.__traverse__`. Both traverse the same `Arc<CombinedValidator>`, so refcounts get incremented twice. That corrupts things enough to crash — SIGSEGV in release builds, abort in debug builds.

I saw this personally: debug build abort after a few iterations, release build segfault. The reporter said django-ninja hits this on every failed request.

The fix is straightforward — remove the redundant traversal:

- `ValidatorCallable` (function.rs): dropped `__traverse__` entirely. The parent `FunctionWrapValidator` already traverses the validator tree, so `ValidatorCallable` doesn't need to.
- `ValidatorIterator` (generator.rs): removed the `self.validator.py_gc_traverse()` call but kept `self.iterator.py_gc_traverse()`. The iterator traversal is needed for GC correctness (it holds Py references), but the validator traversal was the duplicate one.

I tested by running 500 iterations of wrap-validator validation with forced errors in a Python debug build — no abort. Also ran the existing wrap validator tests, they pass. The custom test I wrote exercises the exact scenario from the bug report.

title: Fix #13817: remove double-visitation of validator tree in ValidatorCallable and ValidatorIterator
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #13817 by removing `__traverse__` from `ValidatorCallable` and removing the validator traversal from `ValidatorIterator.__traverse__`
- Prevents double-visitation of the `Arc<CombinedValidator>` tree which corrupted refcounts and caused crashes (SIGSEGV in release, abort in debug builds)

## Root Cause

When a `ValidatorCallable` or `ValidatorIterator` is kept alive (e.g. in a traceback after a `ValidationError`), Python's GC traverses both the parent validator (which traverses the `Arc<CombinedValidator>` via `impl_py_gc_traverse!`) and the child wrapper (which traverses the same `Arc<CombinedValidator>` via its own `__traverse__`). This double-visitation increments refcounts twice, corrupting them and leading to crashes.

## Changes

- **`ValidatorCallable`** (function.rs): Removed `__traverse__` entirely
- **`ValidatorIterator`** (generator.rs): Removed `self.validator.py_gc_traverse()` call, kept `self.iterator.py_gc_traverse()` which is needed for GC correctness

## Testing

- Custom test: 500 iterations of mode='wrap' validation with forced errors — no crash
- Existing wrap validator tests: pass
- Python debug build: no abort

title: Add JSON benchmarks for document shapes the suite does not cover
body:
## Problem

The suite's JSON coverage is narrow in terms of what the documents are *made of*.

`test_north_star_validate_json` is the only realistic JSON validation benchmark, and about a tenth of it is the JSON parse — the rest is UUID, `Decimal`, date/time and discriminated-union work. It is a good instrument for that, and it cannot isolate anything else. Beyond it:

- no file in `tests/benchmarks/` or `tests/pydantic_core/benchmarks/` contains a single non-ASCII character
- nothing has long text fields
- nothing is dominated by floating-point numbers
- the large nested object graph and the repeated-key cases exist only as hand-built microbenchmarks

So the cost of *handling the document* — decoding strings, validating UTF-8, parsing numbers, building and walking the value graph — is currently measured only incidentally, as about a tenth of one benchmark.

## What this adds

Twelve benchmarks over six documents. Each is dominated by one property of the input rather than by the schema, and the models are deliberately plain, so the cost lands in handling the document.

| document | what it is | size | non-ASCII | parse share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `twitter` | real API output; the model reads a subset of the fields, as application code does | 632 KB | 5.6% | 77% |
| `canada` | GeoJSON, ~111k floats and almost nothing else | 2.25 MB | 0% | 57% |
| `catalog` | long prose fields, mostly ASCII with an accented minority | 807 KB | 0.5% | 53% |
| `i18n_users` | eight scripts, the shape of a product with international users | 466 KB | 20.3% | 50% |
| `event_log` | short repeated keys and short ASCII values, the shape of log ingestion | 187 KB | 0% | 32% |
| `citm_catalog` | a large, deeply nested object graph of small records | 1.73 MB | 0.01% | 21% |

"Parse share" is `(validate_json − validate_python) / validate_json`, measured as instruction counts on a pinned core: roughly how much of the benchmark is turning bytes into values rather than validating them. north_star is at 10% by the same measure.

That number is the point of the change. A benchmark at 10% parse share turns a 10% parser improvement into 1%, which is inside CodSpeed's noise; the same improvement is 7.7% on `twitter`. Regressions are symmetrical, and at present a parser regression can land with nothing to show it.

Each document is measured with both `validate_json` and `from_json`. They take different paths and a change can move one without the other, so a pair is more informative than either alone.

## Notes

- `twitter`, `canada` and `citm_catalog` come from [nativejson-benchmark](https://github.com/miloyip/nativejson-benchmark) (MIT), which is what `serde_json`, `simdjson`, RapidJSON and orjson benchmark on, so numbers taken on them are comparable with those projects'. They are vendored `xz` compressed, because `check-added-large-files` caps additions at 500 KB and `canada.json` gzips to 592 KB.
- **Nothing about those three has to be taken on trust.** Committing them compressed makes them unreadable in a diff, so `tests/benchmarks/vendored_documents.py` records the upstream URL, the SHA-256 of each document and the SHA-256 of each compressed file, and can check or rebuild them:

  ```bash
  python -m tests.benchmarks.vendored_documents --check   # offline, against the recorded hashes
  python -m tests.benchmarks.vendored_documents           # re-download and rebuild, byte for byte
  ```

  The rebuild is reproducible because the filter chain is pinned in the script rather than taken from a CLI's defaults: `lzma` preset 9 with a CRC-64 check gives identical bytes on Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64, and matches `xz -9`. Verified on both. `test_vendored_documents_match_upstream` runs the offline check in CI.
- `i18n_users`, `catalog` and `event_log` are generated by seeded `faker` on first run and stay gitignored, the same way `north_star_data.json` is. `/tests/benchmarks/*.json` matches direct children only, so no `.gitignore` change is needed. Regeneration is byte-identical, and each generator reseeds itself so the documents do not depend on generation order.
- `ensure_ascii=False` when writing them is load-bearing: the default emits `\uXXXX` escapes, which take the escape path rather than the UTF-8 path, and the non-ASCII documents stop measuring what they were chosen to measure. There is a comment saying so.
- The benchmarks go through `BaseModel` / `TypeAdapter`, the API users actually call, rather than hand-built `core_schema`.

**Cost.** All twelve total about 661M instructions per run, against about 99M for north_star's two JSON benchmarks. `canada` is 370M of that on its own, being 2.25 MB. If that is too much for a per-PR suite, the obvious trim is to take a subset of its 480 polygon rings rather than to drop it — the shape it covers has no other representative — and I am happy to do that.

title: Keep earlier patterns and search semantics for `str_pattern()` in pipelines
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

`str_pattern()` in the experimental pipeline API has two problems. Both are in the `Pattern` branch of `_apply_constraint()`.

1. **A second pattern replaces the first.** When the schema is a `str` schema, the pattern is written into it (`s['pattern'] = constraint`), so a later `str_pattern()` overwrites an earlier one:

   ```python
   from typing import Annotated
   from pydantic import TypeAdapter
   from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

   ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[str, validate_as(str).str_pattern(r'^\d+$').str_pattern(r'^1')])
   ta.validate_python('1abc')
   #> '1abc', expected a validation error (not all digits)
   ```

2. **The fallback check is anchored.** When the pattern can't go on a `str` schema (for example after a custom `transform()`), the Python fallback uses `constraint.match(v)`. That only matches at the start of the string. The `str` core schema searches the whole string instead (`pattern.is_match()` for the Rust engine, `pattern.search()` for the Python engine). So the same pattern gives a different result depending on the step before it:

   ```python
   TypeAdapter(Annotated[str, validate_as(str).str_pattern('b')]).validate_python('abc')
   #> 'abc'
   TypeAdapter(Annotated[str, validate_as(str).transform(str.title).str_pattern('b')]).validate_python('abc')
   #> ValidationError: Value error, Expected ~ b
   ```

The fix sets the pattern on the `str` schema only when no pattern is there yet, and otherwise uses the fallback check. The fallback now uses `search()`, which matches the `str` schema's semantics. Together, these make repeated patterns all apply with the same meaning.

## Related issue number

None. I couldn't find an existing issue or PR for this. #13856 changes the transform fast path in the same file and doesn't overlap.

## Checklist

* [x] The pull request title is a good summary of the changes - it will be used in the changelog
* [x] Unit tests for the changes exist
* [ ] Tests pass on CI
* [x] Documentation reflects the changes where applicable

title: Keep earlier native constraints when a pipeline repeats a constraint
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

In the experimental pipeline API, applying the same kind of constraint twice keeps only the last one when the schema supports the constraint natively. `_apply_constraint()` writes the value straight into the core schema (`s['le'] = le`), so a second `le()` replaces the first one:

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).le(10).le(100)]).validate_python(50)
#> 50, expected a validation error (50 > 10)

TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).multiple_of(2).multiple_of(3)]).validate_python(3)
#> 3, expected a validation error (3 is not a multiple of 2)

TypeAdapter(Annotated[str, validate_as(str).len(0, 3).len(1, 10)]).validate_python('abcdef')
#> 'abcdef', expected a validation error (longer than 3)
```

The same happens with a constraint from the type passed to `validate_as()`. For example, `validate_as(Annotated[int, Interval(le=10)]).le(100)` accepts 50. When the first constraint lives in a Python check (after a transform, for example), both constraints are enforced. So the result depends on whether the constraint fits the core schema.

This change keeps the fast path only when the key isn't already set on the schema. Otherwise it falls back to the existing Python check, so both constraints apply. It covers `gt`/`ge`/`lt`/`le`, `len()`, `multiple_of()` and the timezone constraints. The `str_pattern()` overwrite is the same shape, but its fallback check has a separate problem (it anchors with `re.match()`), so I kept it for a separate PR.

## Related issue number

None. I couldn't find an existing issue or PR for this. #13856 changes the transform fast path in the same file and doesn't overlap.

title: fix: avoid leaking AliasPath root keys into model_extra in model_construct
body:
## Change Summary

When a model field specifies a `validation_alias=AliasPath(...)` and the model is configured with `extra='allow'`, calling `BaseModel.model_construct` previously leaked the root key of the `AliasPath` into `__pydantic_extra__` (and consequently `model_dump()` / `model_dump_json()`), whereas `BaseModel.model_validate` correctly recognized the root key as consumed.

### Cause & Solution
In `BaseModel.model_construct`, string aliases are removed via `values.pop(alias)`, whereas `AliasPath` evaluation uses `alias.search_dict_for_path(values)`, which leaves the input key intact in `values`. When `extra='allow'`, the remaining keys in `values` are assigned to `_extra`.

To fix this with zero unnecessary allocations and full support for multiple fields sharing the same root key:
1. Matched `AliasPath` root keys (`alias.path[0]`) are recorded in `matched_alias_path_roots: set[str] | None` during field extraction.
2. Root keys are popped from `values` only after all fields have been resolved, right before `_extra` assignment. This prevents one field from prematurely removing a shared root required by subsequent fields.
3. Unmatched `AliasPath` keys are not added to `matched_alias_path_roots`, ensuring that genuinely unmapped keys remain in `model_extra`, preserving complete parity with `model_validate`.

### Tests
Added parameterized tests in `tests/test_construction.py` covering:
- Single `AliasPath` with `extra='allow'`
- Multi-segment `AliasPath` (`a.b.c`)
- `AliasPath` sequence indexing (`items[1]`)
- `AliasChoices` containing an `AliasPath`
- Multiple fields sharing the same `AliasPath` root key
- Unmatched `AliasPath` retaining extra keys
- Immutability of caller's input dictionary
- Exact parity assertion with `model_validate`

## Change Summary

In `pydantic._internal._fields.resolve_default_value`, `smart_deepcopy` was imported inside the function body on every invocation:

```python
def resolve_default_value(...):
    from ._utils import smart_deepcopy
```

Because it was a relative import (`from ._utils import smart_deepcopy`), CPython executed relative module resolution on every single default evaluation during `FieldInfo.get_default` and `BaseModel.model_construct`.

`_fields.py` already imports from `._utils` at module level (line 28). Moving `smart_deepcopy` to the existing module-level import eliminates the per-call import overhead without introducing circular dependencies.

title: Attribute-docstring inspection raises TypeError while cloudpickle reconstructs a local model in a fresh worker

labels.name: bug V2
labels.description: Bug related to Pydantic V2

body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

# Description

A model defined inside a function in a normally imported module cannot be
restored by cloudpickle in a fresh interpreter where that module is unavailable
when it inherits `use_attribute_docstrings=True`. The producer succeeds;
the worker raises `TypeError: <class 'model_defs.Config'> is a built-in class`.
The class is not a built-in class.

I expect unavailable source to produce no extracted attribute descriptions,
just as it does when source inspection raises `OSError`, rather than preventing
reconstruction of an otherwise serializable model. Disabling attribute-docstring
extraction before constructing the producer's model makes the same transfer work.
This reproduction uses only Pydantic and cloudpickle.

## Root cause and proposed fix

Cloudpickle reconstructs local classes by value. Creating the skeleton child
class invokes Pydantic's metaclass before cloudpickle restores its full state.
The parent already enables attribute-docstring extraction, so field collection
calls `extract_docstrings_from_cls()`.

On Python 3.13, that function calls `inspect.getsourcelines(cls)`. When the
class's module is unavailable, Python's `inspect.getfile()` raises `TypeError`.
Pydantic catches `OSError` at this location but not `TypeError`.

Proposed change in `pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py`, scoped only to
retrieving source:

```diff
 try:
     source, _ = inspect.getsourcelines(cls)
-except OSError:
+except (OSError, TypeError):
     return {}
```

I verified this change in an isolated process using Pydantic 2.13.5: the worker
then restores the model and its value successfully. Installed dependency files
were not modified. No claim is made that this resolves every dynamic-class
serialization problem.

## Related issue and duplicate search

[Pydantic #12389](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12389) reports the
same inspection exception during manual `importlib` loading. It was closed with
advice to register the module in `sys.modules` or use normal importing.

This reproduction already imports the producer module normally and asserts
that it is registered in `sys.modules`. Its local classes are serialized by
value; the worker intentionally has no access to their defining module. No
`__module__` rewriting or manual `importlib` loading is involved.

A search on 2026-09-25 for
`repo:pydantic/pydantic "use_attribute_docstrings" "cloudpickle"` found no
matching issue. Searching for `"built-in class" "docstrings"` found #12389;
I did not find an exact report for this worker reconstruction case.

# Example Code

Create the following layout in an empty directory:

```text
producer/
    model_defs.py
    produce.py
worker/
    consume.py
```

`producer/model_defs.py`:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


def make_model(*, use_attribute_docstrings: bool = True) -> type[BaseModel]:
    class Parent(BaseModel):
        model_config = ConfigDict(use_attribute_docstrings=use_attribute_docstrings)

    class Config(Parent):
        value: int = 1
        """A documented field."""

    return Config
```

`producer/produce.py`:

```python
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import cloudpickle
import model_defs

assert sys.modules["model_defs"] is model_defs
Config = model_defs.make_model(use_attribute_docstrings="--no-docstrings" not in sys.argv)
Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1].joinpath("worker/payload.pkl").write_bytes(
    cloudpickle.dumps(Config(value=7))
)
print("producer succeeded")
```

`worker/consume.py`:

```python
from importlib.util import find_spec
from pathlib import Path

import cloudpickle

assert find_spec("model_defs") is None
config = cloudpickle.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("payload.pkl").read_bytes())
assert config.value == 7
print("worker succeeded")
```

From the directory containing `producer/` and `worker/`, run with Python 3.13:

```console
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install pydantic==2.13.5 cloudpickle==3.1.2
.venv/bin/python producer/produce.py
.venv/bin/python worker/consume.py
```

The producer prints `producer succeeded`. The worker's `find_spec` assertion
passes, then unpickling fails. Ensure the `producer/` directory is not added to
`PYTHONPATH`; script execution adds it only to the producer's import path.

Observed traceback on 2.13.5 (environment paths normalized):

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<repro>/worker/consume.py", line 7, in <module>
    config = cloudpickle.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("payload.pkl").read_bytes())
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/cloudpickle/cloudpickle.py", line 553, in _make_skeleton_class
    skeleton_class = types.new_class(
        name, bases, {"metaclass": type_constructor}, lambda ns: ns.update(type_kwargs)
    )
  File "<python>/lib/python3.13/types.py", line 75, in new_class
    return meta(name, resolved_bases, ns, **kwds)
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_model_construction.py", line 243, in __new__
    set_model_fields(cls, config_wrapper=config_wrapper, ns_resolver=ns_resolver)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_model_construction.py", line 579, in set_model_fields
    fields, pydantic_extra_info, class_vars = collect_model_fields(
                                              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        cls, config_wrapper, ns_resolver, typevars_map=typevars_map
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_fields.py", line 423, in collect_model_fields
    _update_fields_from_docstrings(cls, fields)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_fields.py", line 122, in _update_fields_from_docstrings
    fields_docs = extract_docstrings_from_cls(cls, use_inspect=use_inspect)
  File "<repro>/latest/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py", line 99, in extract_docstrings_from_cls
    source, _ = inspect.getsourcelines(cls)
                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^
  File "<python>/lib/python3.13/inspect.py", line 1245, in getsourcelines
    lines, lnum = findsource(object)
                  ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^
  File "<python>/lib/python3.13/inspect.py", line 1060, in findsource
    file = getsourcefile(object)
  File "<python>/lib/python3.13/inspect.py", line 963, in getsourcefile
    filename = getfile(object)
  File "<python>/lib/python3.13/inspect.py", line 932, in getfile
    raise TypeError('{!r} is a built-in class'.format(object))
TypeError: <class 'model_defs.Config'> is a built-in class
```

## Passing control and workaround

Regenerate the payload with source inspection disabled on the parent model:

```console
.venv/bin/python producer/produce.py --no-docstrings
.venv/bin/python worker/consume.py
```

Both commands succeed, and the worker prints `worker succeeded`. This disables
a documentation feature rather than addressing the exception handling. It must
be chosen before producing the model; changing an environment variable in the
consumer does not reconfigure an arbitrary serialized Pydantic model.
Making the defining module importable in the worker is another possible
application-level approach when that deployment constraint is acceptable.

title: `model_construct` with `validation_alias=AliasPath(...)` and `extra='allow'` leaves the alias path keys in `model_extra`
body:
### Description

`BaseModel.model_construct` does not process `validation_alias`, which is expected — `model_construct` takes field names directly and skips validation. But when a field declares `validation_alias=AliasPath(...)` and the model config sets `extra='allow'`, the alias path keys are not removed from the values dict before it is stored as `_extra`. The constructed model's `model_extra`, and its serialization, then contain keys that were only ever there to satisfy the alias path.

`model_validate` with the same model and same input does not leak these keys. The two construction paths disagree.

This is a long-standing behaviour of `model_construct`, not a recent change. It reproduces on the installed release `pydantic 2.13.5` (pydantic_core 2.46.5), Python 3.12.

### Example Code

```python
from pydantic import AliasPath, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Outer(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')

    x: int
    a: dict = Field(validation_alias=AliasPath('a', 'b'))


data = {'x': 1, 'a': {'b': 1}, 'c': 9}

m = Outer.model_validate(data)
print('model_validate  extra:', m.model_extra)

c = Outer.model_construct(**data)
print('model_construct extra:', c.model_extra)
print('model_construct dump :', c.model_dump())
print('model_construct dump_json:', c.model_dump_json())
```

### Observed output

```
model_validate  extra: {'c': 9}
model_construct extra: {'a': {'b': 1}, 'c': 9}
model_construct dump : {'x': 1, 'a': {'b': 1}, 'c': 9}
model_construct dump_json: {"x":1,"a":{"b":1},"c":9}
```

### Expected Behaviour

`model_construct` should not store the alias path portion of the input in `model_extra`. `model_construct` takes field names rather than aliases, so the `a` entry is not an extra key — it is the field declared with `validation_alias=AliasPath('a', 'b')`. The expectation for the output above:

```
model_construct extra: {'c': 9}
model_construct dump : {'x': 1, 'a': {'b': 1}, 'c': 9}
```

That is, `model_extra` should be `{'c': 9}` only, for parity with `model_validate`.

### Root Cause

In `BaseModel.model_construct`, the code walks the model's fields and removes each field's alias from the values dict before what remains is treated as extras. The three branches are not equivalent.

On the installed release, `pydantic 2.13.5`, in `main.py`:

- lines 344-345: the `field.alias` branch — `values.pop(field.alias)`.
- line 357: the `str` validation alias branch — `values.pop(alias)`.
- line 361: the `AliasPath` branch — `value = alias.search_dict_for_path(values)`.
- line 376: `_extra: dict[str, Any] | None = values if cls.model_config.get('extra') == 'allow' else None`.

On `main` as of `a9a0e1d1`, the same four points are at lines 361-362, 374, 378 and 393 respectively.

What differs is the shape of the operation. The first two branches `pop` from `values`, so a key consumed through `field.alias` or through a `str` `validation_alias` is gone by the time `_extra` is assigned. The `AliasPath` branch calls `search_dict_for_path`, which removes nothing: it traverses and returns. By the time line 376 (2.13.5) / 393 (`main`) assigns `_extra`, the path keys the `AliasPath` branch consumed are still in `values`, and with `extra='allow'` those entries become `model_extra`.

`search_dict_for_path` is read-only. In `aliases.py` its body is `v = d`, then a loop of `v = v[k]`, then `return v` — line 39 on the installed 2.13.5, line 38 on `main` at `a9a0e1d1`. There is no mutation and no `pop`, so the fix belongs in `model_construct`'s `AliasPath` branch rather than in the helper.

Controls, all executed against the reproduction above:

| variant | leaks? |
|---|---|
| `AliasPath('a','b')` + `extra='allow'` | yes |
| `AliasPath('a','b','c')` | yes |
| `AliasPath('a', 0)` | yes |
| `AliasPath` inside `AliasChoices` | yes |
| `validation_alias='a'` (str) — control | no |
| no `extra='allow'` | no |
| plain field-name fallback | no |

`model_validate` does not leak in any of these rows.

### Blast Radius

Narrow. Three conditions are required together:

1. the field uses `validation_alias=AliasPath(...)`, not a `str` alias;
2. the model config sets `extra='allow'`;
3. the model is built with `model_construct`, not `model_validate`.

`model_validate` is unaffected in every configuration tested.

The caller's input dict is **not** mutated — neither for `model_construct(**src)` nor for `model_construct(mapping)`. `search_dict_for_path` does not write to the dict it is given, and nothing else in the path removes keys from the caller's object. The stray key is confined to the constructed model: it appears in `model_extra` and in `model_dump` / `model_dump_json`, and does not leak back out to the caller's data.

One further edge: if the field name collides with the path root, the field is also dropped from the dump.

On duplicate search: I did not find an existing report for this. `#8266` is closed and different — `model_construct` not storing non-allowed extras, no `AliasPath`, no `extra='allow'`. `#11046` is closed and different — an `AliasChoices` `KeyError` in `model_construct`, a different failure mode. `#12884` is the nearest open issue, but it is an alias/name collision during serialization and names neither `AliasPath` nor `model_construct`; mentioning it as a possible cross-reference only, not as the same issue.

### Python/Pydantic/OS Version

- pydantic 2.13.5 (installed release)
- pydantic_core 2.46.5
- Python 3.12

The same source locations are present on `main` at `a9a0e1d1`, at the line numbers given in Root Cause.

### AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to prepare this report, including the reproduction script and the control variants. Every output quoted above was produced by executing the code, and the line numbers were read from the installed 2.13.5 sources and from `main` at `a9a0e1d1`.

title: multiple_of=0 still raises ZeroDivisionError for non-native numeric types

labels.name: bug V2

body:
### Description

`Field(multiple_of=0)` is rejected during schema generation for `int`, `float`, and `Decimal`, but equivalent non-native numeric types still pass schema generation and raise an uncaught `ZeroDivisionError` during validation.

### Reproduction

```python
from fractions import Fraction
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Model(BaseModel):
    value: Fraction = Field(multiple_of=0)

Model(value=Fraction(1, 2))
```

Actual: validation raises `ZeroDivisionError` rather than `ValidationError`.

Expected: model definition fails with a schema-generation error stating that `multiple_of` must be greater than zero, consistently with native numeric types.

The Python fallback in `pydantic/_internal/_validators.py` performs `x % multiple_of` without validating the divisor. `Fraction`, temporal types, and `complex` use this fallback. I found no existing report for the remaining types after the native numeric fix.

title: `FieldInfo.get_default` is 5-6x slower on 2.13 because of a relative import in the function body
body:
`FieldInfo.get_default()` costs about five to six times more on 2.13 than on 2.12.

On 2.13 the call is delegated to `pydantic._internal._fields.resolve_default_value`, whose body starts with a relative import that runs on every call:

```python
def resolve_default_value(...):
    from ._utils import smart_deepcopy
```

On 2.12 the plain-default branch was `return _utils.smart_deepcopy(self.default)`, with no import at call time. In 2.13 the import sits before the `default_factory` branch, so every call pays it.

`_fields.py` already has a module-level import from `._utils`, so the in-body import is not breaking an import cycle, and moving the name up adds nothing to import time.

Measured with `timeit`, best of 5 runs of 200000 calls:

| | 2.12.3 | 2.13.5 | 2.13.5, import moved up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FieldInfo(default=123)` | 55 ns | 300 ns | 85 ns |
| `FieldInfo(default_factory=list)` | 35 ns | 271 ns | 60 ns |

The cost is the import statement rather than module loading, since the module is already in `sys.modules`. With the relative form, `resolve_name` runs before the `sys.modules` lookup, so it is paid on every call even though the module is cached. A three-function package, identical except for the import form used to obtain the same callee:

| form | per call |
| --- | --- |
| `from ._helper import work` inside the body | 234 ns |
| `from pkg._helper import work` inside the body | 108 ns |
| module-level import | 32 ns |

Moving the import up removes most of the gap but not all of it. What is left is the extra `resolve_default_value` call and the sentinel checks added to `smart_deepcopy`.

This is visible in `model_construct()`, where `get_default` runs once per field. For a five-field model with defaults: 1.18 us on 2.12.3 against 2.49 us on 2.13.5. Passing every field explicitly, so that no default is resolved, gives 1.12 us on both.

### Version info

pydantic 2.13.5, CPython 3.13, macOS on arm64. The in-body import is still on `main`. Not measured on Linux or x86_64, so the absolute numbers will differ there, though the ratios should hold.
