title: `SerializeAsAny` fails on a deferred model: `TypeError: 'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'`

labels.name: bug V2
labels.description: Bug related to Pydantic V2

body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Serialization with `SerializeAsAny` fails when the runtime class of the value is a deferred model.
A deferred model is a model with `defer_build=True` that pydantic did not build yet.
The call raises this error:

```
PydanticSerializationError: Error serializing to JSON: TypeError: 'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'
```

I expect pydantic to build the deferred model at first use, and then serialize the value.

### Cause

The cause is in pydantic-core, in `src/serializers/infer.rs`.
The function `serialize_pydantic_serializable` reads the attribute `__pydantic_serializer__` from the value.
On a deferred model, this attribute holds a `MockValSer` object, not a `SchemaSerializer` object.
The code downcasts the object to `SchemaSerializer`.
The downcast fails, and the error goes to the caller.

`MockValSer` has a lazy rebuild hook in `__getattr__`.
A Python method call starts this hook.
A Rust downcast does not start this hook.
As a result, the same deferred instance serializes correctly through a direct `model_dump_json()`, but fails through `SerializeAsAny`.
The example code below shows this asymmetry.

### Impact

This failure occurred for us in production.
A worker process serialized instances of model classes that it never validated in that process.
Each `model_dump_json()` call on the parent model failed.

### Versions tested

The failure occurs on all versions that we tested:

- pydantic 2.12.5 / pydantic-core 2.41.5
- pydantic 2.13.4 / pydantic-core 2.46.4
- pydantic 2.14.0b1 / pydantic-core 2.48.0

### Related issues

- #7713 tracks `MockValSer` errors in general.
- #12282 reported this failure and was closed as a duplicate.

### Proposed fix

I have a fix with tests ready on a fork.
The fix changes `get_pydantic_serializer` in `infer.rs`:

1. The function downcasts the attribute value to `SchemaSerializer` as before.
2. If the downcast fails, the function calls the `rebuild()` method of the mock object.
3. The function then uses the serializer that `rebuild()` returns.
4. An object without a `rebuild()` method keeps the current downcast error.

`serialize_pydantic_serializable` and `PolymorphismTrampoline` use the same code path, so one change repairs both.
All pydantic and pydantic-core test suites pass with the fix.
Please assign this issue to me, and I will open the pull request.


### Example Code

```Python
from typing import Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, SerializeAsAny


class Child(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(defer_build=True)
    x: int = 1


class Sub(Child):
    y: int = 2


class Parent(BaseModel):
    content: Optional[SerializeAsAny[Child]] = None


# model_construct() does not validate, so pydantic does not build Sub.
# This is equal to a process that serializes a class that it never validated.
sub = Sub.model_construct(x=1, y=2)
parent = Parent.model_construct(content=sub)
assert Sub.__pydantic_complete__ is False

# 1) The SerializeAsAny path fails on the deferred model.
try:
    parent.model_dump_json()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    # PydanticSerializationError: Error serializing to JSON: TypeError:
    # 'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'

# 2) The direct Python path rebuilds the same deferred model and succeeds.
print(sub.model_dump_json())  # {"x":1,"y":2}
assert Sub.__pydantic_complete__ is True

# 3) After the rebuild, the SerializeAsAny path also succeeds.
print(parent.model_dump_json())  # {"content":{"x":1,"y":2}}
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```Text
pydantic version: 2.14.0b1
        pydantic-core version: 2.48.0
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.11.15 (main, Mar 25 2026, 02:58:47) [Clang 22.1.1 ]
                     platform: macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: unknown

The same example also fails on these versions:
- pydantic 2.13.4 / pydantic-core 2.46.4 (latest stable)
- pydantic 2.12.5 / pydantic-core 2.41.5
```

title: Fix TypeError on unhashable annotations in match_type deprecated-alias lookup
body:
## Change Summary

`match_type` added an unguarded `typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)` lookup in 2.14 that assumes the annotation object is hashable. A `TypeAliasType` subscripted with a `ParamSpec` list argument (e.g. `Alias[[], int]`, common with PEP 695 `type Alias[**P, R] = ...` syntax) is a `types.GenericAlias` whose `__args__` contain a `list`, making it unhashable — so building a schema for any model containing such an annotation crashed with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. Regression vs 2.13.4.

This guards the lookup with `try/except TypeError`, matching the existing guard around `self._handlers.get(obj)` a few lines below. An unhashable object cannot be a `DEPRECATED_ALIASES` key by construction, so skipping the lookup is always correct.

Adds a regression test using `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType` so it runs on all supported Python versions.

## Related issue number

Fixes #13645 (real-world impact: broke `import giskard.checks` under 2.14.0b1, see Giskard-AI/giskard#2719)

title: TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' in match_type for PEP 695 aliases with a ParamSpec (regression in 2.14.0b1)
body:
Reported downstream in Giskard-AI/giskard#2719 (breaks `import giskard.checks`); repro and analysis below. The report was drafted jointly with @davidberenstein1957, who invited it to be filed upstream as-is.

### Description

`_generate_schema.match_type` added an unguarded dict lookup in 2.14 that assumes the annotation object is hashable. It is not, for a PEP 695 type alias with a `ParamSpec` parameterized by an empty list. Schema building for any model containing such an annotation crashes.

This is a regression: the same code builds fine on 2.13.4.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Any
from pydantic import BaseModel

type Alias[**P, R] = Any

class M(BaseModel):
    f: Alias[[], int] | None = None
```

Raises immediately at class-definition time:

```
File ".../pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py", line 1127, in match_type
    if origin is not None and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'
```

### Mechanism

`Alias[[], int]` is a `types.GenericAlias` whose `__args__` is `([], int)`. Hashing the alias hashes that tuple, which contains a `list` — so it is unhashable. The line at `_generate_schema.py:1127`

```python
if origin is not None and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
```

calls `.get(obj)` without checking that `obj` can be hashed. `dict.get` propagates the `TypeError` rather than treating an unhashable key as absent.

### Suggested fix

Guard the lookup, e.g.

```python
if origin is not None and isinstance(obj, Hashable) and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
```

or wrap it in `try/except TypeError`. An unhashable object cannot be a `DEPRECATED_ALIASES` key by construction, so skipping the lookup is always correct.

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

- pydantic 2.14.0b1 (fails) / 2.13.4 (works)
- Python 3.12.13
- Reproduced on Linux and macOS

### Real-world impact

Hit in [giskard-oss](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/giskard-oss), where `type GeneratorType[**P, R, S] = ...` parameterized as `GeneratorType[[], InputType, None]` makes `import giskard.checks` fail outright under 2.14.0b1. Instrumenting `match_type` confirms the offending object:

```
OFFENDING obj  = GeneratorType[[], InputType, None]
OFFENDING type = <class 'types.GenericAlias'>
OFFENDING args = ([], InputType, None)
```

There is no workaround on the library side short of pinning `pydantic<2.14` (done in Giskard-AI/giskard#2752), which is what downstream has had to do.

title: apply UrlConstraints to already-parsed url instances
body:
## Change Summary

`UrlConstraints` writes `allowed_schemes` / `max_length` / `host_required` onto the inner url core schema that `_BaseUrl` and `_BaseMultiHostUrl` wrap. The wrap validator short-circuited with `if isinstance(v, source): return v`, so when the input was already a url object (not a string) the inner schema never ran and none of those constraints applied. `AnyUrl('http://evil.com')` passes an `Annotated[AnyUrl, UrlConstraints(allowed_schemes=['https'])]` field even though the string `'http://evil.com'` is correctly rejected. It is reachable without constructing urls by hand: `Tight.model_validate(loose.model_dump())` hits it because python-mode `model_dump()` keeps the live url instance, and `revalidate_instances='always'` does not help.

The fix runs the instance's already-parsed core url (`v._url`) through the inner schema so the constraints are enforced, then keeps the existing behavior of returning the same object when it already matches the target type, which preserves the documented subclass/identity pass-through (`TypeAdapter(AnyUrl).validate_python(any_http_url) is any_http_url`). Passing `v._url` rather than re-parsing `str(v)` avoids an extra parse on that hot path. Same change in both `_BaseUrl` and `_BaseMultiHostUrl`.

title: fix(docs_extraction): preserve docstrings from parent classes across hierarchy including TypedDict
body:
## Summary

Addresses issue 13468.

When \use_attribute_docstrings=True\ is set, fields inherited from a parent \TypedDict\ (or stdlib dataclass hierarchy) previously lost their docstring descriptions in the subclass JSON schema. This occurred because \extract_docstrings_from_cls\ only inspected the immediate subclass's AST rather than traversing parent bases in the class hierarchy (and \TypedDict\ classes store parent bases in \__orig_bases__\).

This PR:
1. Adds a \_get_class_hierarchy\ helper to traverse parent class bases (handling \__orig_bases__\ for \TypedDict\).
2. Targets specific \st.ClassDef\ nodes per base class to extract docstrings in reverse inheritance order (allowing subclasses to override parent field docstrings).
3. Resolves existing \xfail\ test \	est_stdlib_docs_extraction_inheritance\ and adds \	est_typeddict_docs_extraction_inheritance\.

## Test Plan

title: Return `NotImplemented` from URL equality comparisons with foreign types
body:
## Change Summary

`_BaseUrl.__eq__` and `_BaseMultiHostUrl.__eq__` return `False` for an operand of a different class:

```python
def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
    return self.__class__ is other.__class__ and self._url == other._url
```

`False` tells Python the comparison succeeded, so the reflected `__eq__` on the other operand is never consulted and `==` becomes asymmetric:

```python
from unittest.mock import ANY
from pydantic import AnyUrl

AnyUrl('https://example.com') == ANY   # False
ANY == AnyUrl('https://example.com')   # True
```

The practical fallout is the usual assertion shape `assert result == {'url': ANY, ...}`: dict comparison evaluates the left dict's value first, so the URL is on the left and the assertion fails. `BaseModel` does not have this problem — `BaseModel.__eq__` returns `NotImplemented  # delegate to the other item in the comparison` — so the same assertion behaves differently depending on whether the field value is a model or a URL.

`NotImplemented` is what the data model asks for here, and it is what `dataclasses` generates. It is also the reasoning that got `BaseModel.__eq__` changed in #5622.

The fix mirrors what #13495 did for the four ordering comparators:

```python
def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
    if self.__class__ is not other.__class__:
        return NotImplemented
    return self._url == other._url
```

#13495 scoped `__eq__` out on the grounds that "equality against a foreign type is well defined and correctly returns `False`". That holds for the direct comparison, but not for the reflected one above.

Observable behaviour is otherwise unchanged. For operands with no cross-type equality of their own (`str`, `int`, `None`, another URL class) the reflected `__eq__` also returns `NotImplemented`, Python falls back to identity, and the result is still `False` — `AnyUrl('https://a.com') != 'https://a.com'` and `AnyUrl('https://a.com') != HttpUrl('https://a.com')` still hold, and the existing assertions in `test_any_url_ordering_is_consistent` pass unmodified. `__hash__` is untouched, so hashing, set dedup and dict lookup are unaffected.

### Tests

Two tests in `tests/test_networks.py`, both failing on `main` and passing here:

- `test_any_url_equality_delegates_to_foreign_type` — a cooperative wrapper type compares equal to a URL from either side, for both `_BaseUrl` and `_BaseMultiHostUrl`; `str` and `int` still compare unequal.
- `test_any_url_equality_with_mock_any` — `unittest.mock.ANY` matches in both directions, including nested in a dict.

Full `tests/test_networks.py`: 310 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

## Related issue number

None — I found no open issue or PR covering URL `__eq__`. Follow-up to #13495; same class of bug as #5622, which was fixed for `BaseModel`.

title: Remove look-around assertions from Decimal JSON schema patterns
body:
### Change Description

The JSON schema `pattern` generated for `Decimal` fields uses negative look-around assertions (`(?!...)`). The regex engine used for validation does not support look-around, so pydantic rejects its own generated pattern when it is reused as an explicit `pattern` constraint:

```python
schema = Foo.model_json_schema()
RootModel[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=schema['properties']['bar']['anyOf'][1]['pattern'])]].model_validate_json('"1.4"')
# -> SchemaError: regex parse error ... look-around, including look-ahead
```

This PR rewrites the Decimal patterns without look-around by enumerating the significant-digit alternatives explicitly. The accepted/rejected value sets are unchanged — verified by fuzzing 50k+ strings against the previous patterns across all `max_digits`/`decimal_places` combinations, and by the existing `test_decimal_pattern_*` suites.

title: JSON schema discriminator mapping uses Python-style `True`/`False` keys for `bool` discriminators
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When a discriminated union uses a `bool` discriminator (`Literal[True]` / `Literal[False]`), the generated JSON schema's `discriminator.mapping` uses the Python string representations `"True"` and `"False"` as keys:

```json
"discriminator": {
    "mapping": {"False": "#/$defs/Disabled", "True": "#/$defs/Enabled"},
    "propertyName": "enabled"
}
```

Per the [OpenAPI discriminator specification](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0#discriminator-object), mapping keys must match the serialized payload value of the discriminator property. For a boolean property, that value serializes to JSON `true`/`false`, so the keys should be `"true"` and `"false"`. Tooling that resolves the mapping against the payload (code generators, validators such as openapi-generator or Redocly) fails to match either variant.

Expected:

```json
"mapping": {"false": "#/$defs/Disabled", "true": "#/$defs/Enabled"}
```

Note that `Enum` discriminator keys are already normalized to their value (`k.value`) before stringification in `GenerateJsonSchema.tagged_union_schema`; `bool` keys just fall through to `str(k)`.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Enabled(BaseModel):
    enabled: Literal[True]
    config: str


class Disabled(BaseModel):
    enabled: Literal[False]


class Model(BaseModel):
    setting: Enabled | Disabled = Field(discriminator='enabled')


print(Model.model_json_schema()['properties']['setting']['discriminator'])
# {'propertyName': 'enabled', 'mapping': {'True': '#/$defs/Enabled', 'False': '#/$defs/Disabled'}}
```

title: Replace `impl_py_gc_traverse!` with a `#[derive(PyGcTraverse)]` macro traversing all fields
body:
Second approach to address #13625.

## What this does

Replaces the `impl_py_gc_traverse!` macro (and most hand-written `PyGcTraverse` impls) with a `#[derive(PyGcTraverse)]` proc macro, implemented in a new `pydantic-core-derive` workspace crate. The derive traverses **every** field by default:

- A field whose type doesn't implement `PyGcTraverse` is a **compile error**, forcing an explicit decision: derive on that type, add a no-op impl for plain data, or mark the field `#[py_gc(skip)]`.
- Skips are explicit, greppable, and reviewable. The entire codebase ends up with exactly **two**, both commented: the partially-uninitialized `RecursionStack::Array` buffer and `GenericIterator::JsonArray` (JSON data can't hold Python references).
- `py_gc.rs` gains no-op impls for primitives and plain external types (jiter/speedate/regex), plus container impls (`AHashSet`, `OnceLock`, `SmallVec`, 2-tuples).

Nice consequences of the migration:

- The hand-written 50-variant `CombinedSerializer` match ("implemented by hand because `enum_dispatch` fails") is now a derive.
- `EnumValidator<T>`'s four per-instantiation macro calls collapse into one generic derive.
- ~270 lines net deleted.

## Bugs this found and fixed

Migrating exposed real, previously-unknown leaks — every field the derive newly traverses was reviewed:

1. **`GeneralFieldsSerializer.extra_serializer`** was not traversed: serializer functions in `extras_schema` leaked (also caught by #13626's check; not covered by #13624). Fixed automatically by the derive.
2. **`StrConstrainedValidator`'s compiled pattern**: with `regex_engine='python-re'`, the validator holds a `Py<PyAny>` compiled pattern (`RegexEngine::PythonRe`) that was never reported to the GC. Fixed automatically by the derive.

## One trap worth reviewing closely

`DefinitionRefValidator`/`DefinitionRefSerializer` previously had deliberately *empty* traverse lists — they are the cycle-breakers for recursive schemas. Deriving all fields made them traverse `DefinitionRef<T>`, whose (previously unreachable) manual impl recursed into the definition target → infinite recursion → segfault on recursive schemas.

The fix makes `DefinitionRef<T>`'s traversal an explicit documented no-op: it is sound because every definition's content is already traversed through the `Definitions` container held by the top-level `SchemaValidator`/`SchemaSerializer`, and it removes the landmine for any future struct holding a `DefinitionRef`.

## Validation

- pydantic-core suite: 5616 passed (including `test_garbage_collection.py`), pydantic suite: 7930 passed.
- The `gc.get_referents()` completeness check (from #13626) passes for all five known leak scenarios: the three #13621 edges, `extra_serializer`, and the `python-re` pattern.
- `cargo clippy` clean (lib, tests, and the derive crate).

## Notes

- The derive crate is a path dependency; if pydantic-core is still published to crates.io, the crate needs publishing too (version is kept in lockstep) — happy to adjust.
- `/derive` is added to the sdist `include` list.
- Once PyO3/pyo3#5663 lands upstream, this crate can likely be deleted in favor of the official mechanism.

title: Check GC traversal completeness when constructing validators and serializers in tests

labels.name: relnotes-ignore
labels.description: Omit this PR from the release notes.

body:
First approach to address #13625.

Part of #13625, defense-in-depth against bugs like #13621.

Every `SchemaValidator`/`SchemaSerializer` construction during the pydantic-core test suite now verifies that the Python objects retained from the core schema are reported to the garbage collector, so a field missing from an `impl_py_gc_traverse!()` call fails whichever existing test exercises that schema feature.

## How it works

`gc.get_referents(obj)` returns exactly what `tp_traverse` reports, which allows checking traversal completeness directly, without having to construct an actual leak scenario:

1. Walk the core schema and collect candidate objects (classes, callables, enum members — plain values may be converted on the Rust side and don't necessarily need to be traversed).
2. Construct the validator/serializer; candidates whose `sys.getrefcount()` increased are retained by it.
3. Assert every retained candidate appears in `gc.get_referents()` of the instance (recursing only into plain Python containers).

The retained `py_schema` is deliberately excluded from the reachability walk: reachability through it is not enough for cycles to be collectable, as CPython requires every strong reference held by the Rust structures to be reported individually (this exclusion is what makes the check work at all).

The interception swaps the `SchemaValidator`/`SchemaSerializer` names inside test modules only (after collection, once all test modules are imported), leaving `pydantic_core` itself and other consumers (e.g. `pydantic`) untouched. The check is disabled on non-CPython implementations, on free-threaded builds (`sys.getrefcount()` isn't reliable with deferred reference counting), for benchmarks, and per-test via the new `skip_gc_traverse_check` marker.

## Limitations

- The check is per-object membership, not per-edge counting: an object held via two Rust fields of the same struct with only one traversed would not be flagged. The realistic bug pattern — a new field never traversed anywhere — is caught.
- Candidates are limited to classes, callables and enum members; a missing edge holding e.g. only a plain container would not be flagged.
- Validators/serializers constructed at module import time (before collection finishes) are not checked.

title: Memory leak: transient models using Enum methods or Field(exclude_if=...) survive GC

labels.name: bug V2
labels.description: Bug related to Pydantic V2

body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Transient `BaseModel` classes are not collected when either:
* A model field references an `Enum` whose class defines a Python method.
* A model field uses `Field(exclude_if=<Python callable>)`.

After the defining module is removed from `sys.modules` and every ordinary strong reference is dropped, weak references to the model and enum classes remain alive after repeated full `gc.collect()` calls. Repeating this construction in disposable module namespaces causes linear memory growth.

Controls using an enum without methods or a field without `exclude_if` are collected normally.

I encountered this in combination with a Temporal workflow sandbox. With a large interconnected model graph and high volume Temporal workflows this can result in multi-GiB process growth relatively quickly.

The likely cause is missing `PyGcTraverse` edges for Python objects held by pydantic-core:
* `SerField` owns `serialization_exclude_if`, but traverses only `serializer`: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/c67a1397327c6abc1a2e2e921af01aebbbeedf1c/pydantic-core/src/serializers/fields.rs#L26-L38
* `EnumSerializer` owns `class`, but traverses only `serializer`: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/c67a1397327c6abc1a2e2e921af01aebbbeedf1c/pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/enum_.rs
* Each `EnumValidator<T>` owns `lookup`, but traverses only `class` and `missing`: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/c67a1397327c6abc1a2e2e921af01aebbbeedf1c/pydantic-core/src/validators/enum_.rs

Traversing `py_schema` does not compensate for another unreported direct reference: CPython’s collector accounts for every actual strong edge individually.

I tested a temporary build from Pydantic `main` at `c67a1397327c6abc1a2e2e921af01aebbbeedf1c`. Adding only these traversal edges made all objects in the reproduction collectible:
* Add `serialization_exclude_if` to `SerField` traversal.
* Add `class` to `EnumSerializer` traversal.
* Add `lookup` to every `EnumValidator<T>` traversal.

For the enum case, changing only the serializer or only the validator was insufficient; both missing edges were required.

This appears related to earlier missing-traversal fixes such as:

* https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/5136
* https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/787
* https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1100

I would be happy to submit a focused patch.

(please note that this analysis was LLM assisted)

### Example Code

```Python
import gc
import sys
import types
import weakref

def transient_module(name, source, class_names):
    module = types.ModuleType(name)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    exec(compile(source, f"<{name}>", "exec"), module.__dict__)
    refs = tuple(
        weakref.ref(module.__dict__[class_name])
        for class_name in class_names
    )
    del sys.modules[name]
    del module
    return refs

enum_ref, enum_model_ref = transient_module(
    "_pydantic_enum_gc_repro",
    """
from enum import Enum
from pydantic import BaseModel
class Membership(str, Enum):
    FULL = "full"
    def label(self) -> str:
        return self.value
class Model(BaseModel):
    membership: Membership
""",
    ("Membership", "Model"),
)

(exclude_if_model_ref,) = transient_module(
    "_pydantic_exclude_if_gc_repro",
    """
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
class Model(BaseModel):
    value: int = Field(exclude_if=lambda value: False)
""",
    ("Model",),
)

for _ in range(5):
    gc.collect()

# All three should be False because no intentional strong references remain.
print("enum alive:", enum_ref() is not None)
print("enum model alive:", enum_model_ref() is not None)
print("exclude_if model alive:", exclude_if_model_ref() is not None)
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

## Change Summary

Infer a `defaultdict` value factory for the concrete types `dict` and `frozenset`.

`collections.abc.Mapping` / `MutableMapping` already mapped to `dict`, and `collections.abc.Set` already mapped to `frozenset`, but the concrete types themselves were missing from the inferred-factory allow list. This is the same hole as `list` / `set` / `tuple` already being listed next to their ABCs. Nested `defaultdict` still requires an explicit factory.

title: Reject trailing input and non-ASCII digits in `ByteSize`
body: ## Change Summary `ByteSize` parses a size string in `ByteSize._validate` with `byte_string_re.match()` against `^\s*(\d*\.?\d+)\s*(\w+)?`. The pattern has no end anchor and `.match()` only pins the start, so any content after a valid `` prefix is silently dropped: `'1kb; rm -rf /'`, `'1kb\nHost: evil'`, and `'1kb">'` all validate to `1000`. In a `str` pattern `\d`/`\w` are Unicode-aware and `str.lower()` is a full case fold, so the scalar and unit accept non-ASCII spellings too: `'٤kb'` (Arabic-Indic four) parses to `4000`, `'１kb'` (fullwidth one) to `1000`, and a KELVIN SIGN unit folds to `k`. The fix compiles `byte_string_re` with a trailing `\s*$` anchor and the `re.ASCII` flag, so the value has to be a complete, ASCII-only size string. The check sits on the parser because `ByteSize` is the trust boundary and a field typed `ByteSize` can't sanitize the raw value first; the core `str_schema` pattern stays as the coarse pre-filter. It tightens validation, so a few previously accepted malformed inputs now raise `byte_size`, while every well-formed value including surrounding whitespace still parses to the same result. ## Related issue number None; found while reading the `ByteSize` parser. ## Checklist * [x] The pull request title is a good summary of the changes - it will be used in the changelog * [x] Unit tests for the changes exist * [x] Tests pass on CI * [ ] Documentation reflects the changes where applicable * [x] My PR is ready to review, **please add a comment including the phrase "please review" to assign reviewers**

title: Preserve `re.Pattern` instance for compiled patterns in the experimental pipeline

labels.name: relnotes-fix
labels.description: Used for bugfixes.

body: in `_apply_constraint`, a compiled `Pattern` constraint on a string schema was folded in as `s['pattern'] = constraint.pattern`, which keeps only the source string and drops the `re` flags. pydantic-core's regex defaults are not python's (`\w`/`\d`/`\b` are unicode-mode), so a pattern built with `re.ASCII` stops being ascii-only: `validate_as(str).constrain(re.compile(r'^\w+$', re.ASCII))` lets a cyrillic `аdmin` through, and `re.IGNORECASE` gets dropped the other way and rejects valid input. the string schema already accepts a compiled pattern and honors its flags, which is how `StringConstraints` passes one through, so this hands `constraint` over instead of its source. flag-free patterns (including `str_pattern`) fold identically to before; the regression test pins the re.ASCII and re.IGNORECASE cases.

title: Fix `exclude`/`include` ignored with `model_serializer(when_used="json")` in python mode
body:
## Change Summary

Fix `exclude`/`include` being silently ignored when a model uses `@model_serializer(when_used="json")` (or any non-`always` `when_used`) and `model_dump()` is called in **python** mode.

**Root cause** (in `pydantic-core`, Rust): the `function_type_serializer!` macro — shared by `FunctionPlainSerializer` and `FunctionWrapSerializer` — unconditionally called `state.scoped_include_exclude(IncludeExclude::empty())` after `self.call()`, regardless of whether the user's serializer function was actually invoked. When `when_used` does not match (e.g. `when_used="json"` but mode is `python`), the function is skipped and the fallback serializer is used. Because include/exclude was reset to empty on this fallback path, the model-level `exclude`/`include` was silently dropped.

**Fix**: the `scoped_include_exclude(IncludeExclude::empty())` call is now applied only on the `Ok((true, v))` branch (function was called — it owns filtering via the `SerializationCallable`). On the `Ok((false, v))` fallback branch the original `state` is passed through unchanged, so the fallback serializer correctly applies `exclude`/`include`.

This affects all three serialization entry points (`to_python`, `json_key`, `serde_serialize`) and both `mode="wrap"` and `mode="plain"` model serializers. Field serializers were already correct (the model-level filter is applied before the field serializer is reached, so resetting the field-level scope to empty was a no-op).

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, model_serializer

class Gated(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: int

    @model_serializer(mode="wrap", when_used="json")
    def ser(self, handler, info):
        return handler(self)

# Before (python mode): {'a': 1, 'b': 2}  — exclude ignored
# After:                 {'a': 1}
assert Gated(a=1, b=2).model_dump(exclude={"b"}) == {"a": 1}
```

Fix #13601

title: Allow access to strict-mode JSON type coercions after JSON decode
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

Context/Background:
Reported issue: https://github.com/psalvaggio/dynapydantic/issues/33
and the fix I came up with: https://github.com/psalvaggio/dynapydantic/pull/34

To distill the above context to a smaller reproducer:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter, ValidationError

class Model(BaseModel, strict=True):
    file_path: Path

adapter = TypeAdapter(Model)

decoded_json = {
    "file_path": "/tmp/example.txt",
}

# This is the value a field-level validator receives after
# model_validate_json() has decoded the JSON document.
try:
    adapter.validate_python(decoded_json, strict=True)
except ValidationError as exc:
    print("validate_python failed:")
    print(exc)

# Pydantic's JSON validation accepts the same string in strict mode
# and performs the JSON-specific Path coercion.
result = adapter.validate_json(
    '{"file_path": "/tmp/example.txt"}',
    strict=True,
)

print(result)
# Model(file_path=PosixPath('/tmp/example.txt'))
```

Given the constraints I have in my library, it would be desirable to be able to access the available type coercions in strict-mode JSON validation from the TypeAdapter. I could see this taking one of two forms:

1. Allow `strict` on `validate_python` to also take `"json_strict"` or something like that. This is appealing as a non-breaking API change.
2. Allow `validate_json` to take an already decoded object. This seems less desirable.

title: Fix callable discriminators on PEP 695 type aliases
body:
## Change Summary

Fix callable discriminators applied with `Field(discriminator=...)` to PEP 695 type aliases.

A tagged alias such as:

```python
type FooBar = Annotated[Foo, Tag('foo')] | Annotated[Bar, Tag('bar')]

class Model(BaseModel):
    value: FooBar = Field(discriminator=Discriminator(get_type))
```

raised `callable-discriminator-no-tag` even though both choices had tags. The field path supplied the alias definitions to `apply_discriminator()`, but the callable branch discarded them before `_convert_schema()`, so the alias `definition-ref` could not be resolved to its tagged union.

The fix threads the existing definitions mapping into `_convert_schema()` and resolves the root reference before building the tagged union. A focused regression test covers both choices using native PEP 695 syntax.

## Change Summary

In the model metaclass, prior to the class being created, we fetch annotations to perform checks. This is a bit fragile (although the logic in this PR still is fragile for annotations _not_ fully evaluated) because in Python < 3.14, we fetch the raw `__annotations__`, and in Python >= 3.14, this requires evaluating annotations (and we'll end up doing it again in `collect_model_fields()`). An added test show a case where we now correctly classify an attribute as being private.

This also unifies exceptions to use `PydanticUserError` instead of bare `TypeError`/`NameError`.

title: Fix model validators called twice with recursive models
body:
Fixes #13581

## Root cause

When a model references an already-built recursive model, the schema inlines the recursive model's definition as `function-after(model(...))` (or `function-wrap`). The prebuilt-validator guard added for #11505 rejects reuse when the class's root validator is `FunctionWrap`/`FunctionAfter`, but for recursive models the root validator is a `DefinitionRef` pointing at those wrappers. The guard missed it: the inner `model` schema was replaced by the full prebuilt validator (wrappers included) and the referencing schema applied the wrappers a second time, running `wrap`/`after` model validators twice per instance.

## Fix

Peek through the `DefinitionRef` before the guard check via a new `read_definition` accessor on `DefinitionRefValidator` (`definitions.rs`). Prebuilt reuse is preserved for recursive models without `wrap`/`after` model validators.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

class NodeVal(BaseModel):
    value: int
    child: 'NodeVal | None' = None

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def validate_node(self) -> 'NodeVal':
        print(f'validator called (value={self.value})')
        return self

class OuterVal(BaseModel):
    root: NodeVal

# Before: prints "validator called" twice
# After:  prints "validator called" once
OuterVal(root={'value': 1})
```

## Notes

- `before` validators are unaffected (single call, unchanged behavior)
- The serializer side has an analogous issue (`wrap` model serializers on recursive models run twice via `CombinedSerializer::Recursive`) - left as a follow-up to keep this change focused
- 2 regression tests added next to the existing #11505 tests (`test_recursive_model_after_val_called_once`, `test_recursive_model_wrap_val_called_once`)

## Tests

434 `tests/test_validators.py` + `tests/test_main.py`, 158 pydantic-core prebuilt/validator tests, 410 across `test_edge_cases`, `test_serialize`, `test_forward_ref`, `test_construction` - all pass.

title: fix: prevent duplicate model validator execution on recursive models (#13581)
body:
### Selected PR Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update

### Summary of Changes
Fixes #13581: Validators called twice with recursive models.

#### Root Cause
Previously, `apply_model_validators(..., 'outer')` in `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py` wrapped `model_schema` in a `function-after` schema, placing `ref` on `function-after` instead of the underlying `model_schema`. When `pydantic-core` validated a `definition-ref` pointing to `function-after`, it executed `function-after` and then re-validated the returned model instance because the root definition schema was `function-after` rather than `type: 'model'`.

#### Fix
- Applied model validators to `inner_schema` prior to constructing `core_schema.model_schema` in `_generate_schema.py`.
- Preserves `model_schema` at the root of definition references, eliminating duplicate validator executions during model validation.
- Added unit test `test_recursive_model_validator_single_execution` in `tests/test_model_validator.py`.

### Verification
- Verified that validating recursive models (e.g. `OuterVal.model_validate({'node': {}})` where `NodeVal` references itself) executes `@model_validator(mode='after')` exactly once.

body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Part of https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13173 (just adding CI support).

---

I'm not sure what to do about the `base64` changes in the stdlib, which affects our `Base64UrlBytes` type:
1. [`base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/base64.html#base64.urlsafe_b64decode) now raises a deprecation warning when `+` and `/` is present in the input (the point being that users of this function are expected to pass an input that is using `-` and `_` instead). 
    However, our docs currently say:

    https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/5f49d856043b668321b44f56ed8c440f750bd76b/pydantic/types.py#L2840-L2844
   I don't really understand the last sentence, it seems that we explicitly documented `urlsafe_b64decode()`'s behavior when `+` and `/` are present in input, and that they would be accepted.

2.  [`base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/base64.html#base64.urlsafe_b64decode) no longer requires the input to be padded. There's no explanation for this change. [python/cpython#73613 (comment)](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/73613#issuecomment-4171000832) says:

    > The default value is True, except in `base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`. So, padding of input no longer required in `base64.urlsafe_b64decode()` by default.

More generally, we will likely be subject to these kind of changes in the future (e.g. https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148204), and I'm not sure what should be done in these cases (we can try to preserve backwards compatibility on our side -- with non trivial workarounds e.g. for the change 1. -- or follow what the stdlib does, but with expected breaking changes).

title: Require types passed to `GenerateSchema.generate_schema()` to be evaluated
body:
## Change Summary

`generate_schema()` previously resolved forward references lazily on every node: `_get_args_resolving_forward_refs()` inspected (and possibly re-evaluated) the arguments of every parametrized container, union, `Annotated` form and tuple, and `_generate_schema_inner()` handled `str`/`ForwardRef` inputs. After auditing all callers, types reaching `generate_schema()` are in practice already fully evaluated, so this per-node machinery is removed and evaluation is enforced at the entry points instead:

- **Callers already passing evaluated types** (no change): model/dataclass fields (guaranteed by `__pydantic_fields_complete__`/rebuild), TypedDict/NamedTuple annotations, `validate_call` argument annotations, PEP 695 type alias values.
- **`TypeAdapter`**: the adapted type is now evaluated upfront with `_typing_extra.eval_type()` (`NameError` is converted to `PydanticUndefinedAnnotation`, preserving the defer-build/mock/rebuild flow, e.g. `TypeAdapter('MyType', config=ConfigDict(defer_build=True))`).
- **`validate_call`**: the return annotation is now evaluated with `get_function_type_hints()`, as was already done for argument annotations in `_call_schema()`.

The main blocker was Python 3.10, where `typing._eval_type()` doesn't evaluate *string* arguments of PEP 585 generic aliases (e.g. `list['Foo']`, fixed in 3.11 by python/cpython#30900) — exactly what the lazy resolution was compensating for. This is now handled at evaluation time in `_typing_extra._eval_type()`, by recursively converting such arguments to `ForwardRef` instances and re-applying evaluation when a forward reference resolves to an alias itself containing string arguments (implicit recursive aliases like `Json = list['Json']` still raise the friendly `RecursionError`).

`_resolve_forward_ref()` is kept, but only for annotations that are lazily provided *by design* and can only be evaluated during schema generation, behind `isinstance(..., (str, ForwardRef))` guards:

- `json_schema_input_type` and serializer/computed field `return_type` values provided as strings,
- type variable bounds/constraints/defaults (e.g. `TypeVar('T', bound='Element')`),
- types passed as strings to the public `handler.generate_schema()`, and incomplete stdlib dataclass field annotations (via `CallbackGetCoreSchemaHandler`).

Minor behavior changes:

- On 3.10, the "Unable to evaluate type annotation" error message for `list['CustomType[int]']` now matches 3.11+ (test updated).
- An unresolvable `validate_call` *return* annotation now raises `NameError` (consistent with argument annotations) instead of `PydanticUndefinedAnnotation`.

### Performance

Profiling a module importing a large number of models (~590 top-level schema builds): cumulative time spent in `generate_schema()` drops from 113ms to 98ms (~13%), from no longer running the per-argument `ForwardRef` checks/resolution on every type node. Overall import wall-clock improves ~1–3%.

title: Allow arbitrary core schemas for serialization
body:
As per the TODO in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/13487:

There is currently no way to tell `pydantic-core` "serialize this value using this core schema". `Ser`Schema is:

```python
SerSchema = Union[
    SimpleSerSchema,
    PlainSerializerFunctionSerSchema,
    WrapSerializerFunctionSerSchema,
    FormatSerSchema,
    ToStringSerSchema,
    ModelSerSchema,
]
```

The only member that expresses "use this schema" is `SimpleSerSchema`, and it does not take a schema at all, only a name from a closed literal:

```python
ExpectedSerializationTypes = Literal[
    'none', 'int', 'bool', 'float', 'str', 'bytes', 'bytearray', 'list', 'tuple',
    'set', 'frozenset', 'generator', 'dict', 'datetime', 'date', 'time', 'timedelta',
    'url', 'multi-host-url', 'json', 'uuid', 'any',
]

class SimpleSerSchema(TypedDict, total=False):
    type: Required[ExpectedSerializationTypes]
```

So an arbitrary schema (a model, a dataclass, `list[int]`, a TypedDict, anything constructed by the schema generator) cannot be used directly. Every place in Pydantic that needs it works around the gap the same way: it wraps the schema in a wrap serializer whose function is the identity, purely so the schema can ride along in the `schema` argument.

From `ValidateAs.__get_pydantic_core_schema__()`:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/27f95c789b20aa23306e5ce559327db0e9a10a6e/pydantic/functional_validators.py#L911-L917

Changelog

Sourced from cryptography's changelog.

50.0.0 - 2026-07-31


* **SECURITY ISSUE**:
  :func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
  and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors or
  timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which could
  act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted messages.
  A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-69247**
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
  ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification <cryptography.x509.verification>` APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
  <https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption>`_ for streaming authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
  carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
  ``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
  ``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER form,
  matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
  :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a request
  or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version defined
  by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now supported

title: Fix documented default of `ConfigDict.str_min_length`
body:
## Change Summary

`ConfigDict.str_min_length` is annotated `int` and its actual default is `0` (`config_defaults` in `pydantic/_internal/_config.py`), but the docstring says "Defaults to `None`" — `None` isn't even a legal value for the annotation. Looks copied from the `str_max_length: int | None` entry directly below, where `None` is correct.

Since this docstring is rendered as the `ConfigDict` API reference, the published docs currently state an impossible default. One-line docstring fix, no runtime change.

body:
This is a poor man's version of https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12575, which does not introduce any new API for core schema generation, and instead focuses only on performance of core schema generation type dispatching.

By taking the proper steps at "decomposing" the arbitrary annotation passed to `generate_schema()`, we can avoid repeated calls to `get_origin()`, `typing._GenericAlias.__eq__()` (all the `obj` in `*_TYPES` calls), etc.

Closes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/13541 (better performance here, and better approach too).

Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

## Change Summary

`field_title_generator` is documented in `pydantic/fields.py` as "A callable that takes a field name and returns title for it", in the docstrings of `Field()`, `FieldInfo.from_field()`, `computed_field()` and `ComputedFieldInfo`. from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

```python
#> TypeError: <lambda>() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given
```

`ConfigDict.field_title_generator` already documents it correctly, so this aligns the four `fields.py` docstrings with that wording.

title: Pipeline API raises `SchemaError` for numeric constraints not coercible to the schema type
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Since #13516, a numeric constraint in the pipeline API whose bound is not losslessly coercible to the schema's numeric type raises a `SchemaError` when the validator is built. The same pipelines validated correctly before that commit.

`_apply_constraint()` previously called `_check_func()` unconditionally for `Ge`, `Lt`, `Le` and `MultipleOf`, so a non-integral bound on an `int` schema was enforced by the Python predicate. #13516 moved those calls into `else:` branches, which correctly removes the double application, and replaced the per-type narrowing with a direct assignment to the core schema. The bound now reaches `pydantic-core`, which rejects it:

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).ge(2.5)])
```

Current `main`:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.SchemaError: Error building "int" validator:
  ValueError: 'ge' must be coercible to an integer
```

On `dc484e211` (immediately before that PR) the validator builds and behaves correctly, rejecting `2` and accepting `3`.

The same applies to `.le(5.5)`, `.lt(5.5)`, `.multiple_of(2.5)`, `.constrain(Interval(ge=0.5, le=9.5))` and `.le(float('inf'))` on an `int` schema, and to non-`float` bounds on a `float` schema.

`gt` is not a regression: its `_check_func()` call was already in an `else:` branch, so a non-integral bound was previously dropped silently and the constraint was not enforced at all. #13516 turned that silent no-op into an error.

The comment added in #13516, "No casting of the constraints is necessary, as pydantic-core does it when building the validator from the core schema", holds while the bound is losslessly coercible, but not otherwise.

The tests added in that PR cover integral floats only (`.ge(0.0)`, `.le(5.0)`, `.gt(0.0)`, `.multiple_of(5.0)`), which are coercible, so this is not caught.

Before attempting a PR: is raising here the intended behaviour, matching `Annotated[int, Ge(2.5)]` which also raises, or should the `_check_func()` fallback be kept when the bound cannot be applied to the core schema?

### Example Code

```Python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

# Each of these raises SchemaError on main, and builds on dc484e211:
TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).ge(2.5)])
TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).le(5.5)])
TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).multiple_of(2.5)])
TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).le(float('inf'))])
```

body:
## Change Summary

A computed field using `exclude_if` is still listed in the serialization JSON Schema `required` array, even though serialization may omit it:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field

class Model(BaseModel):
    a: int = Field(default=0, exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)

    @computed_field(exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)
    @property
    def b(self) -> int:
        return 0

print(Model().model_dump())
#> {}
print(Model.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')['required'])
#> ['b']
```

#12430 handled this for regular fields in `GenerateJsonSchema.field_is_required()`, and #12748 later added `exclude_if` support to computed fields without touching `pydantic/json_schema.py`. `_name_required_computed_fields()` still hardcodes `True`, so the sibling path was missed.

title: Fix `KeyError` when a custom `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` returns embedded `$defs`
body:
## Change Summary

A custom `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` may return a JSON schema that carries its **own** `$defs` and internal `$ref`s. Pydantic's JSON-schema assembly assumed every `$ref` resolves in its own definitions registry, so `TypeAdapter(...).json_schema()` crashed with `KeyError: '#/$defs/...'`.

Minimal repro (from #12145):

```python
from typing import Any
from pydantic import GetCoreSchemaHandler, GetJsonSchemaHandler, TypeAdapter
from pydantic.json_schema import JsonSchemaValue
from pydantic_core import core_schema

class CarDict:
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type: Any, handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler):
        return core_schema.dict_schema(keys_schema=core_schema.str_schema(), values_schema=core_schema.any_schema())
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_json_schema__(cls, cs, handler: GetJsonSchemaHandler) -> JsonSchemaValue:
        return {
            '$defs': {'Tire': {'properties': {'brand': {'title': 'Brand', 'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['brand'], 'title': 'Tire', 'type': 'object'}},
            'properties': {'tires': {'items': {'$ref': '#/$defs/Tire'}, 'title': 'Tires', 'type': 'array'}},
            'required': ['tires'], 'title': 'Car', 'type': 'object',
        }

TypeAdapter(CarDict).json_schema()  # KeyError: '#/$defs/Tire'
```

### Fix

Three read-only passes — `get_schema_from_definitions`, `get_json_ref_counts`, and `_garbage_collect_definitions` — look each `$ref` up in `self.json_to_defs_refs`. They already tolerate external `http(s)://` refs they don't own, but re-raised on **local** refs they don't own. A `$ref` that resolves in neither the registry nor as an external URL points into a user-embedded `$defs`; pydantic doesn't manage it, so these passes now skip it (it is walked inline and passes through to the output unchanged) rather than crash.

The change is symmetric across the three sites and leaves behavior for pydantic-owned and external refs untouched.

## Related issue number

fix #12145

body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

I have a wrap validator that rounds the decimal places down to `decimal_places` passed in a `Field()` annotation.
However, i noticed, that this doesn't work if  `WrapValidator()` is followed by `Field()`. It does work if `Field()` is followed by `WrapValidator()`, or if i assign `Field()`, however former prevents me from annotating `Decimal` with validator for reuse, and latter is a legacy notation.

Print statements show that `handler` doesn't actually respect `Field()` constraints if it is placed after the `WrapValidator()`.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, WrapValidator, ValidationError, ValidationInfo, ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler, Field
from typing import Any, Annotated
from decimal import Decimal

def round_decimal(value: Any, handler: ValidatorFunctionWrapHandler, info: ValidationInfo) -> Decimal:
    print(f"> {info.field_name}\nIn: {value}")
    try:
        result = handler(value)
    except ValidationError as err:
        exc = err.errors()[0]
        if exc["type"] == "decimal_max_places":
            ctx = exc["ctx"]  # pyright: ignore[reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess]
            result = round(value, ctx["decimal_places"])
        else:
            raise
    print(f"Out: {result}\n")
    return result.normalize() + 0

RoundedDecimal = Annotated[Decimal, WrapValidator(round_decimal)]

class Test(BaseModel):
```

title: Fix `max_digits`/`decimal_places` for high-precision decimals
body:
## Change Summary

Both decimal constraint validators normalize the value before counting its digits, only to discount trailing zeros, but `Decimal.normalize()` runs in the active decimal context:

- with the default `prec=28` a longer value is rounded before it is counted, so `Decimal('1.' + '1' * 40)` (41 significant digits, 40 decimal places) satisfies `max_digits=30` and `decimal_places=30`
- the strictness of the check therefore tracks `decimal.getcontext().prec`, which is thread-local and can be changed by anything else in the process
- a value outside the context's `Emax`/`Emin` signals instead of returning, so `Decimal('1E+1000000')` raises `decimal.Overflow` out of the validator, which only catches `TypeError`

The fix drops trailing zeros directly on the `as_tuple()` representation, with no context involved and nothing to signal. An earlier revision normalized in a fixed `Context(prec=MAX_PREC, Emax=MAX_EMAX, Emin=MIN_EMIN)`, but the pure Python `decimal` (the only implementation on PyPy) can construct exponents beyond any context's bounds, so a wide context still signaled there; the `as_tuple()` form closes that as well. Values with trailing zeros, e.g. `Decimal('1.230')` against `max_digits=3, decimal_places=2`, are still discounted as before.

These validators are reached when the constraint can't be pushed into the core decimal schema, e.g. `Annotated[Decimal, AfterValidator(...), Field(max_digits=30)]`. Two things reviewers should weigh:

- this is a behavioral tightening: values that previously passed only because context rounding shrank them below the limit before counting are now rejected
- the plain-field path in `pydantic-core` (`src/validators/decimal.rs`) calls `normalize()` with no context argument, so it rounds to the active `prec` the same way this code did; after this change the two paths disagree on such values until core gets the same treatment. I'm happy to file the core counterpart if you'd rather they move together.

title: Tracking: model build memory & startup optimizations (#13522, #13523, #13529, #13530, #13540–#13542, #13544)
body:
Tracking issue for the model-build memory & startup optimization PRs opened this week. The table below is the short version: what each PR buys, so it's easy to see what is given up by not landing any one of them. Measured numbers follow. (#13528, boxing oversized `CombinedValidator` variants, already merged and isn't listed.)

## The PRs, and what each one buys

| PR | What it changes | What you give up if it doesn't land |
|---|---|---|
| #13522 | Prebuilt validator/serializer reuse is silently disabled by *any* installed plugin (e.g. an unconfigured logfire), and refused for models with `model_validator(mode='after'/'wrap')` / `model_serializer(mode='wrap')` | **~57 MB (−36%) of the google-genai import** for any app with a pydantic plugin installed. Also a correctness fix: on released 2.13.4, `after`/`wrap` model validators/serializers run **twice** on recursive models when reached through a referencing model |
| #13523 | `gather_schemas_for_cleaning()` walked shared schema objects once per *path* — exponential for interconnected models | Interconnected-model codebases hit an exponential cliff: a 300-model reference chain is **unbuildable today, 0.86 s with the PR** |
| #13529 | Store `FieldInfo._attributes_set` compactly (flat tuple, dict materialized lazily) | ~60% of that structure's memory: google-genai's 2,707 fields go **498 KB → 201 KB** |
| #13530 | Share structurally identical `nullable`/`default` validator & serializer nodes within a schema build | **−21% import RSS** on repetitive `Optional`-heavy model sets (2,000 models × 20 `Optional[str]` fields: 121 → 95 MB); ~neutral on google-genai, whose field shapes rarely repeat |
| #13540 | Micro-optimizations: core-config construction, deprecated-method identity checks, per-field decorator filtering | **~3–5%** of per-model class-definition time |
| #13541 | Replace `match_type()`'s comparison chain with a dict dispatch | **~5–8%** of per-model class-definition time |
| #13542 | Cache the generated core schema of "pure" annotations (annotations provably unaffected by hooks or config) | **~15–20%** of per-model class-definition time on plain-annotation shapes (up to **×2.3** on pydantic's own CodSpeed benchmarks). Doesn't cover `Annotated`/constrained fields — #13544 adds those |
| #13544 | Fast paths for fields that are a pure annotation + simple default: `FieldInfo` templates, whole `model-field` node cache, annotation-eval skip, trusted stdlib/URL leaf classes. Stacked on #13542 | The largest single build-time PR: **another ~20%** on top of #13542 on every shape, and the only one that moves `Annotated`/constrained fields (**−21%** there) |

All four build-time PRs together (#13540+#13541+#13542+#13544): **24–36% less per-model class-definition time than released 2.13.4**, depending on field shape.

## Build-time numbers, measured against released 2.13.4

Median per-model class-definition cost, µs. 600 models × 3 fields per sample, fresh interpreter per sample, 15 samples per cell, all configs interleaved round-robin. Python 3.14.4; "released" = pydantic 2.13.4 + pydantic-core 2.46.4 wheels from PyPI; the branch configs run over one shared release-profile locally-built core. `main @ 35b8d94` (the branches' base) measures within noise of released 2.13.4 on all three shapes, so the per-PR columns read the same against either baseline.

| shape | released 2.13.4 | main @ 35b8d94 | #13540 | #13541 | #13542 | #13542+#13544 | all four |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `f: Optional[str] = None` | 228 | 224 | 217 | 208 | 184 | 149 | **146 (−36%)** |
| `f: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10)] = 'x'` | 346 | 339 | 328 | 332 | 334 | 264 | **263 (−24%)** |
| mixed (int / Optional / Union / Annotated / float) | 217 | 229 | 207 | 213 | 183 | 146 | **148 (−32%)** |

Real-library imports, same protocol (wall time and peak RSS; mcp 2.0.0 defines ~640 models, google-genai 1.72.0 defines 766):

| | released 2.13.4 | all four PRs | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import mcp` | 428 ms / 70.5 MB | 397 ms / 71.1 MB | **−7% wall**, +0.6 MB |
| `import google.genai` | 732 ms / 105.2 MB | 715 ms / 106.6 MB | −2% wall (within noise), +1.4 MB |

Two honest caveats, so nobody quotes the ×2.3 as a startup number:

- Real imports move by single-digit percentages because model definition is only one slice of an import budget dominated by module bytecode, class creation, Rust validator/serializer construction, and schema-cleaning traversal. Per-PR deltas on whole-library imports are inside machine noise; the per-model table above is where individual attribution is reliable.
- The new caches cost a small bounded amount of memory (+0.6 MB on `import mcp`, +1.4 MB on google-genai, above). They reset above 512 entries; a full google-genai import produces 118 distinct keys, MCP 139.

## The bigger lever: a precompiled schema cache (experiment, not a PR)

The four build-time PRs cut the per-model constant. The dramatic option is to not do the work at import time at all: serialize each model's finished `__pydantic_core_schema__` + `model_fields` at build/install time (like `.pyc` files), and on import deserialize them and hand them straight to the Rust `SchemaValidator`/`SchemaSerializer`.

A feasibility experiment on the MCP SDK (script below):

- **All 613 model classes** defined by `import mcp` serialize cleanly with class/function references tokenized — 0 failures, **1.9 MiB total (~3 KB/model)**.
- Warm-path cost to restore all of them: **~30 ms to deserialize + ~3 ms of Rust validator/serializer builds** (with #13522's prebuilt reuse, referenced models rebuild nearly free, bottom-up).
- That ~32 ms floor replaces **~190 ms of model-definition self-time** in that import (per `-X importtime`, the model-defining modules' slice) — an **~84% reduction ceiling** for the model-build slice, i.e. roughly **160 ms off `import mcp`** — far beyond what incremental per-model work can reach.

What it would take to make real, none of it looking fundamental: resolve tokenized class/function references by qualified name at load; regenerate-and-graft the few closure-bearing subtrees (e.g. URL `wrap` validators); an invalidation key (pydantic version + model source hash); a placeholder fixup for the class object still being created during `ModelMetaclass.__new__`. Flagging explicitly: unlike everything above, this has observable surface (cache files, staleness semantics) and deserves a design discussion before any code — but the ceiling is large enough that it seems worth having that discussion.

<details>
<summary>Feasibility experiment script</summary>

```python
"""Feasibility experiment: what would an on-disk precompiled-schema cache buy for `import mcp`?

Measures, for every model class defined by mcp:
- the cost of serializing/deserializing their core schemas + model_fields (pickle with
  tokenized class/function references, resolved via a lookup table on load — approximating
  a real by-qualified-name resolution),
- the cost of building the Rust validators/serializers from the deserialized schemas,
- compared against the measured model-definition self-time of the import.
"""

import io
import pickle
import sys
import time

t0 = time.perf_counter()
import mcp  # noqa: F401

import_time = time.perf_counter() - t0

from pydantic import BaseModel  # noqa: E402
from pydantic._internal._model_construction import ModelMetaclass  # noqa: E402

# Collect every pydantic model class defined by mcp-related modules:
models = []
seen = set()
for mod_name, mod in list(sys.modules.items()):
    if not mod_name.startswith('mcp'):
        continue
    for obj in list(vars(mod).values()):
        if (
            isinstance(obj, ModelMetaclass)
            and obj is not BaseModel
            and issubclass(obj, BaseModel)
            and id(obj) not in seen
            and obj.__pydantic_complete__
        ):
            seen.add(id(obj))
            models.append(obj)

print(f'models collected: {len(models)}   (import took {import_time * 1000:.0f}ms)')

# --- Serialization: tokenize classes/functions/unpicklable leaves ---
token_table: dict[str, object] = {}


class TokenPickler(pickle.Pickler):
    def persistent_id(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, type) or callable(obj):
            token = f'{id(obj)}'
            token_table[token] = obj
            return token
        return None


class TokenUnpickler(pickle.Unpickler):
    def persistent_load(self, pid):
        return token_table[pid]


def dumps(obj) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    TokenPickler(buf, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL).dump(obj)
    return buf.getvalue()


def loads(data: bytes):
    return TokenUnpickler(io.BytesIO(data)).load()


# Dump schemas + fields:
t0 = time.perf_counter()
blobs = []
failed = 0
for cls in models:
    try:
        blob = dumps({'schema': cls.__pydantic_core_schema__, 'fields': cls.__pydantic_fields__})
        blobs.append((cls, blob))
    except Exception:
        failed += 1
dump_time = time.perf_counter() - t0
total_bytes = sum(len(b) for _, b in blobs)
print(f'dumped {len(blobs)} models ({failed} failed), {total_bytes / 1024:.0f}KiB, dump {dump_time * 1000:.1f}ms')

# Load (median of 3):
load_times = []
for _ in range(3):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    loaded = [loads(b) for _, b in blobs]
    load_times.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
load_time = sorted(load_times)[1]
print(f'unpickle all schemas+fields: {load_time * 1000:.1f}ms')

# Rust validator+serializer build from existing schemas (the part a disk cache can't skip):
from pydantic_core import SchemaSerializer, SchemaValidator  # noqa: E402

from pydantic._internal._config import ConfigWrapper  # noqa: E402

t0 = time.perf_counter()
built = 0
build_failed = 0
for cls, _ in blobs:
    try:
        core_config = ConfigWrapper(cls.model_config, check=False).core_config(title=cls.__name__)
        SchemaValidator(cls.__pydantic_core_schema__, core_config)
        SchemaSerializer(cls.__pydantic_core_schema__, core_config)
        built += 1
    except Exception:
        build_failed += 1
rust_build_time = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'Rust validator+serializer build for {built} models ({build_failed} failed): {rust_build_time * 1000:.1f}ms')

print()
print(f'=> hypothetical warm-cache floor (unpickle + Rust build): {(load_time + rust_build_time) * 1000:.0f}ms')
```

Output (mcp 2.0.0, Python 3.14.4, release-profile core, on top of the four build-time PRs):

```
models collected: 613   (import took 551ms)
dumped 613 models (0 failed), 1910KiB, dump 52.3ms
unpickle all schemas+fields: 29.6ms
Rust validator+serializer build for 613 models (0 failed): 2.6ms

=> hypothetical warm-cache floor (unpickle + Rust build): 32ms
```

</details>

## Landing order and conflicts

**#13540 → #13541 → #13542 → #13544 (stacked on #13542, will be retargeted once it merges), then #13523.** #13522, #13529 and #13530 are independent and can land any time.

The reason #13523 goes last: its CodSpeed report flags −8.4% on `test_simple_recursive_model_schema_generation` — real (the memoization bookkeeping costs about what the skipped traversals save at small schema sizes; the payoff is that the exponential case stops existing). Once #13540–#13542 are in, the same benchmark comes out ahead of today's main, so measuring #13523 against a post-#13542 base avoids the report stalling the PR for nothing.

One known conflict: #13540 ↔ #13544 collide textually in `_fields.py` (adjacent additions, no semantic overlap). Every other pair merges clean.

## Design notes for reviewers

- **Bounded caches**: all new process-wide caches reset once they exceed 512 entries, so dynamically-generated-model workloads can't grow them without bound (measured: 20,000 throwaway models with distinct `Literal`s end up *below* the no-cache baseline RSS).
- **Identity, not equality**: every type-membership test and dispatch table is keyed by `id()`. `in`/`dict.get` on a type is equality-based where the code it replaces was identity-based — a metaclass that makes a class compare equal to `int` must not share `int`'s entry (this also sidesteps unhashable annotations).
- **Order sensitivity**: `typing.Union`/`Literal` hash and compare order-insensitively (`Union[int, str] == Union[str, int]`) while generated schemas are order-sensitive, so annotation objects themselves are unsound cache keys; keys are canonical order-preserving tuples.
- **No partially-built state, no locks**: the caches only store finished results; "pure" annotations are finite trees over builtins with no user hooks, so reentrancy can't observe in-construction state; cache maintenance is single atomic `dict` operations, safe on free-threaded builds.
- **Trusted-class reuse is verified per use**: the #13544 leaf-class cache (UUID, paths, IPs, pydantic URL types) re-checks the class's schema hooks, `_constraints`, and serializer identity on every lookup, so monkeypatching any of them bypasses the cache (covered by tests).

## Measurement protocol

Fresh interpreter per sample; all configs interleaved round-robin so machine-load drift hits every config equally; medians reported. Two traps that produced wrong numbers before they were caught, written down so they aren't rediscovered: `uv run` re-syncs by default and silently rebuilds the editable `pydantic-core` in the debug profile (~9× slower — assert `pydantic_core._pydantic_core.build_profile == 'release'` inside every run); and baselines must be pinned to an explicit SHA, not a moving local `main`.

title: Add fast paths for fields defined by a pure annotation and a simple default
body:
## Change Summary

**Stacked on #13542** (targets that branch; will be retargeted to `main` once it merges — only the last commit is new).

#13542 caches the *inner schema* of repeated pure annotations, but each field still pays for annotation evaluation, `FieldInfo` construction, and the per-field schema scaffolding around the cached part. This PR collapses that remaining pipeline for the most common kind of field — a pure annotation with no metadata and at most a simple immutable default (`str | None = None`, `int`, `Literal['a', 'b'] = 'a'`, …):

- **`FieldInfo` templates**: `collect_model_fields()` copies a cached template instead of re-running `inspect_annotation` + `FieldInfo` construction for every occurrence of the same `(annotation, default)` pair. The actual annotation/default objects are set on each copy, so equal-but-distinct spellings (`Union[int, str]` vs `Union[str, int]`) are preserved on `model_fields`, and instances are never shared between models.
- **Complete field-node cache**: `_generate_md_field_schema()` caches the whole `model-field` node (inner schema, default wrapper, metadata). Eligibility is decided on the `FieldInfo` attributes themselves rather than `_attributes_set`, so attributes set by title/alias generators or by users mutating `model_fields` entries before `model_rebuild()` are respected (covered by tests).
- **Annotation evaluation skip**: `get_model_type_hints()` skips `typing._eval_type()` for pure annotations, which by construction contain no strings or forward references.
- The pure-annotation machinery moves to a new `_internal/_schema_cache.py` module (now shared by `_fields.py`, `_generate_schema.py` and `_typing_extra.py`), and `inspect_namespace()` gains two exact fast paths for the dominant namespace entries.

Default values participating in cache keys are restricted to immutable builtins (`None`/`bool`/`int`/`str`/`bytes` — no `float`, as `0.0`/`-0.0` are equal yet distinguishable), so no mutable default is ever shared.

Measured (release build, fresh interpreter, interleaved A/B on a synthetic benchmark of 600 models × 3 fields; profiled runs confirm e.g. `inspect_annotation` dropping from 1600 calls to 1):

| shape | main | all 4 PRs | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Optional[str] = None` | ~250µs/model | ~140µs/model | **−44%** |
| `int` (required) | 162µs | 112µs | −31% |
| `Union[int, str, None]` | 214µs | 136µs | −36% |
| mixed shapes | 230µs | 178µs | −23% |
| `Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10)]` | 312µs | 321µs | unchanged (metadata bypasses the caches) |

`Annotated`/metadata-carrying fields and string annotations (`from __future__ import annotations` modules) are the natural next extension and are untouched here.

title: Prevent a validator method from overriding an inherited validator of a different kind
body:
## Change Summary

`DecoratorInfos` keys every decorator registry by the **method name** in the class
namespace, and `Decorator.bind_to_cls()` resolves that name again on the class the
decorators are bound to. So when a subclass reuses the name of an inherited validator for
a *different* kind of validator, the inherited entry is rebound to the override and one
method is silently invoked in two different roles.

Using the example from #11299, inspecting the collected decorators on `BrokenModel` shows
both registries pointing at the same function:

```
field_validators['map_foo'] -> func.__qualname__ = BrokenModel.map_foo
model_validators['map_foo'] -> func.__qualname__ = BrokenModel.map_foo
```

The parent's `@field_validator` never runs, and the child's `@model_validator` runs twice
with unrelated inputs (once the whole input dict, once just the field value):

```
('model_validator', {'foo': 'foo'})
('model_validator', 'foo')
```

This adds `DecoratorInfos.find_duplicates()`, which returns the names registered under
more than one kind of validator or serializer, and raises `PydanticUserError` from the
existing `DecoratorInfos._validate()` with a new `validator-method-override` error code:

```
Validator method 'map_foo' overrides an existing validator method, this is not allowed.
```

Overriding an inherited validator with one of the **same** kind only replaces the existing
registry entry, which is ordinary subclassing, so it stays allowed.

### Notes on the previous attempt

This picks up #11782, which was closed without merging. I followed the review feedback
left there by @DouweM:

- the check is a method on `DecoratorInfos` using `self`, named `find_duplicates`, and
  returns a plain list that is built once (no double set conversion),
- there is a comment explaining *why* the clash is a problem rather than just that it is,
- the message is `Validator method {name!r} overrides an existing validator method, this is
  not allowed.`, with a separate message listing all names when several clash,
- a new error code is introduced and documented in `docs/errors/usage_errors.md`,
- the tests assert the exact error message.

One open question from that review was *"Should we also consider that serializer methods
may conflict?"* — **yes**, and this PR covers them. `field_serializers` and
`model_serializers` live in the same name-keyed registries and clash identically. I
verified each combination:

| parent | child | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field_validator` | `model_validator` | `validator-method-override` |
| `model_validator` | `field_validator` | `validator-method-override` |
| `field_validator` | `field_serializer` | `validator-method-override` |
| `field_serializer` | `model_serializer` | `validator-method-override` |
| `field_validator` | `field_validator` | allowed (same kind) |

`computed_fields` is deliberately left out of the check: it is keyed by the property name
rather than a validator method name, and including it is a separate question.

## Related issue number

fix #11299

## Checklist

* [x] The pull request title is a good summary of the changes - it will be used in the changelog
* [x] Unit tests for the changes exist
* [x] Tests pass on CI
* [x] Documentation reflects the changes where applicable

### How this was verified

The five tests that expect the new error fail on `main` with
`Failed: DID NOT RAISE PydanticUserError`, and pass with the change. The two tests that
assert the *allowed* cases pass both before and after, so they act as regression guards
against the check being too broad.

`tests/test_docs.py::test_docs_examples` is skipped on Windows
(`find_examples(..., skip=sys.platform == 'win32')`), so I checked the two new
documentation examples separately against the same rules `run_example` applies — ruff
lint, ruff format at 80 columns with single quotes, and actual execution — and all pass.
